title.zh: 卷一百三十五 列傳第六十 哥舒翰子:曜 高仙芝 封常清
title.en: Volume 135 Biographies 60: Ge Shu Han and son: Yao, Gao Xianzhi, Feng Changqing
title.raw: 卷一百三十五 列傳第六十 哥舒翰子:曜 高仙芝 封常清 Volume 135 Biographies 60: Ge Shu Han and son: Yao, Gao Xianzhi, Feng Changqing

sentences.zh: 哥舒翰子:曜 高仙芝 封常清

translations.literal: Ge Shu Han, son Yao, Gao Xianzhi, Feng Changqing
translations.idiomatic: Ge Shu Han and His Son Yao; Gao Xianzhi; Feng Changqing

sentences.zh: 哥舒翰

translations.literal: Ge Shu Han
translations.idiomatic: Ge Shu Han

sentences.zh: 哥舒翰，其先蓋突騎施酋長哥舒部之裔。

translations.literal: Ge Shu Han — his ancestors were presumably descendants of the Ge Shu clan, chieftains of the Turgesh.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Shu Han's forebears were likely descendants of the Ge Shu branch of the Turgesh chieftains.

sentences.zh: 父道元，為安西都護將軍、赤水軍使，故仍世居安西。

translations.literal: His father Daoyuan served as Protectorate General of Anxi and commissioner of the Chishui Army; therefore the family lived in Anxi for generations.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daoyuan held the posts of Protectorate General of Anxi and commissioner of the Chishui Army, and the family had long resided in Anxi.

sentences.zh: 翰少補效轂府果毅，家富於財，任俠重然諾，縱蒱酒長安市。

translations.literal: When young, Han was appointed a guoyi of the Xiaogu Prefecture; his family was wealthy in property; he was chivalrous and prized his word, and gambled and drank freely in the city of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Han entered service as a guoyi of the Xiaogu Prefecture. His family was rich, he lived by the code of the knight-errant and held his promises sacred, and he spent his days gambling and drinking in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 年四十餘，遭父喪，不歸。

translations.literal: When he was over forty, his father died, and he did not return home.
translations.idiomatic: After he passed forty, his father died, and he did not go home for the mourning.

sentences.zh: 不為長安尉所禮，慨然發憤，遊河西，事節度使王倕。

translations.literal: Not treated with courtesy by the Chang'an district magistrate, he indignantly roused himself to anger, traveled to Hexi, and entered the service of Military Commissioner Wang Chui.
translations.idiomatic: Snubbed by the magistrate of Chang'an, he burned with humiliation, went west to Hexi, and took service under Military Commissioner Wang Chui.

sentences.zh: 倕攻新城，使翰經略，稍知名。

translations.literal: When Chui attacked Xincheng, he had Han oversee operations, and Han gradually became known.
translations.idiomatic: When Chui attacked Xincheng, he put Han in charge of the campaign, and Han's name slowly spread.

sentences.zh: 又事王忠嗣，署衙將。

translations.literal: He later served Wang Zhongsi and was appointed a yamen general.
translations.idiomatic: He later entered the service of Wang Zhongsi and was appointed a yamen general.

sentences.zh: 翰能讀《左氏春秋》、《漢書》，通大義。

translations.literal: Han could read the Zuo Commentary and the Book of Han and grasp their larger meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Han could read the Zuo Commentary and the Book of Han and understood their broader import.

sentences.zh: 疏財，多施予，故士歸心。

translations.literal: He was free with his wealth and gave much away; therefore men gave him their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Generous with his money and liberal in his gifts, he won the loyalty of the men under him.

sentences.zh: 為大鬥軍副使，佐安思順，不相下。

translations.literal: He served as deputy commissioner of the Dadou Army, assisting An Sishun, and the two would not yield to each other.
translations.idiomatic: As deputy commissioner of the Dadou Army under An Sishun, he and his superior were constantly at odds.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣更使討吐蕃，副將倨見，翰怒，立殺之，麾下為股抃。

translations.literal: Zhongsi again sent him to campaign against the Tibetans; a deputy general received him with arrogance, and Han in anger killed him on the spot; his troops clapped their thighs in approval.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongsi sent him against the Tibetans again, a deputy general treated him with insolence. Han flew into a rage and executed him at once, and his soldiers slapped their thighs in delight.

sentences.zh: 遷左衛郎將。

translations.literal: He was promoted to captain of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to captain of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃盜邊，與翰遇苦拔海。

translations.literal: The Tibetans raided the frontier and encountered Han at Kuba Sea.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetans raided the border, they met Han at Kuba Sea.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃枝其軍為三行，從山差池下，翰持半段槍迎擊，所向輒披靡，名蓋軍中。

translations.literal: The Tibetans divided their army into three ranks and came down the mountain in staggered lines; Han took up a half-length spear to meet them, and wherever he turned the enemy broke and scattered; his fame covered the army.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans split their force into three columns and descended the slopes in uneven ranks. Han met them wielding a shortened spear, and wherever he turned the enemy lines crumbled; his renown spread through the whole army.

sentences.zh: 擢授右武衛將軍，副隴右節度，為河源軍使。

translations.literal: He was promoted and appointed General of the Right Martial Guard, deputy military commissioner of Longyou, and commissioner of the Heyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of the Right Martial Guard, made deputy military commissioner of Longyou, and appointed commissioner of the Heyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 先是，吐蕃候積石軍麥熟，歲來取，莫能禁。

translations.literal: Previously the Tibetans had waited until the wheat at Jishi Army ripened and came every year to take it; none could stop them.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, the Tibetans had timed their raids to the ripening of the wheat at Jishi Army and came each year to carry it off, and no one could prevent them.

sentences.zh: 翰乃使王難得、楊景暉設伏東南穀。

translations.literal: Han then had Wang Nande and Yang Jinghui set an ambush in the southeastern valley.
translations.idiomatic: Han then had Wang Nande and Yang Jinghui lay an ambush in the southeastern ravine.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃以五千騎入塞，放馬褫甲，將就田，翰自城中馳至鏖鬥，虜駭走，追北，伏起，悉殺之，只馬無還者。

translations.literal: The Tibetans entered the pass with five thousand horsemen, turned their horses loose and doffed their armor, and were about to go to the fields; Han galloped from the city to join the fierce battle; the barbarians fled in alarm; he pursued them northward, the ambush rose, and all were killed — not a single horse returned.
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand Tibetan horsemen crossed the border, turned their mounts loose, and stripped off their armor to go harvesting. Han galloped out from the fort to join the fight. The enemy fled in panic; he pursued them north until the ambush closed in and wiped them out — not one horse made it back.

sentences.zh: 翰嘗逐虜，馬驚，陷於河，吐蕃三將欲刺翰，翰大呼，皆擁矛不敢動，救兵至，追殺之。

translations.literal: Han once pursued the barbarians; his horse startled and he fell into a river; three Tibetan generals wished to stab Han; Han shouted loudly, and all held their spears and dared not move; rescue troops arrived and pursued and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while pursuing the enemy, Han's horse bolted and he fell into a river. Three Tibetan officers moved to spear him, but Han roared so fiercely that they froze with their weapons raised. When reinforcements arrived, the pursuers were cut down.

sentences.zh: 翰有奴曰左車，年十六，以膂力聞。

translations.literal: Han had a slave named Zuoche, sixteen years old, famed for his bodily strength.
translations.idiomatic: Han kept a slave named Zuoche, sixteen years old and renowned for his brute strength.

sentences.zh: 翰工用槍，追及賊，擬槍於肩，叱之，賊反顧，翰刺其喉，剔而騰之，高五尺許，乃墮，左車即下馬斬其首，以為常。

translations.literal: Han was skilled with the spear; pursuing and overtaking a bandit, he rested the spear on his shoulder and shouted at him; the bandit looked back; Han stabbed his throat, lifted him on the spearhead, and raised him about five feet high, then dropped him; Zuoche immediately dismounted and cut off his head — this became his custom.
translations.idiomatic: Han was a master of the spear. When he overtook a foe, he would level the weapon on his shoulder and shout; as the man turned, Han drove the point into his throat, hoisted him five feet into the air on the shaft, then let him fall. Zuoche would dismount at once and take the head — a routine they performed again and again.

sentences.zh: 會忠嗣被罪，帝召翰入朝，部將請齎金帛以救忠嗣，翰但齎樸裝，曰：「使吾計從，奚取於是？

translations.literal: When Zhongsi fell under accusation, the emperor summoned Han to court; his staff officers asked that he carry gold and silk to save Zhongsi; Han brought only plain dress and said: "If my plan succeeds, what need is there for these?
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongsi was charged with a crime, the emperor summoned Han to court. His officers urged him to bring gold and silk to ransom Zhongsi, but Han took only plain clothes and said, "If my plan works, what need have I of such things?

sentences.zh: 不行，用此足矣。

translations.literal: If it does not, this will suffice.
translations.idiomatic: If it fails, this is enough."

sentences.zh: 」翰至，帝虛心待，與語，異之，拜鴻臚卿，為隴右節度副大使。

translations.literal: " When Han arrived, the emperor received him with an open mind, spoke with him, and was impressed; he was appointed Minister of Ceremonial and deputy grand commissioner of the Longyou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Han arrived, the emperor received him without reserve, spoke with him at length, and was struck by the man. Han was appointed Minister of Ceremonial and deputy grand commissioner of Longyou.

sentences.zh: 翰已謝，即極言忠嗣之枉。

translations.literal: After Han had thanked him, he immediately spoke at length of Zhongsi's injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Once the audience was over, Han immediately pleaded at length that Zhongsi had been wronged.

sentences.zh: 帝起入禁中，翰叩頭從帝，且泣。

translations.literal: The emperor rose and entered the inner palace; Han kowtowed and followed the emperor, weeping as he went.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rose and withdrew into the inner palace. Han kowtowed and followed him, weeping as he went.

sentences.zh: 帝寤，為末貸其罪，忠嗣不及誅。

translations.literal: The emperor came to himself and at the last pardoned Zhongsi's crime; Zhongsi escaped execution.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented and finally commuted Zhongsi's sentence, and Zhongsi was spared execution.

sentences.zh: 朝廷稱其義。

translations.literal: The court praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised him for his loyalty and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 逾年，築神威軍青海上，吐蕃攻破之。

translations.literal: The next year he built the Shenwei Army on the Qinghai; the Tibetans broke through and destroyed it.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he built the Shenwei Army on the Qinghai, but the Tibetans overran and destroyed it.

sentences.zh: 更築于龍駒島，有白龍見，因號應龍城。

translations.literal: He built again on Dragon Colt Island; a white dragon appeared, and therefore it was named Fortress of the Responding Dragon.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt on Dragon Colt Island, where a white dragon was seen, and the post was therefore named Fortress of the Responding Dragon.

sentences.zh: 翰相其川原宜畜牧，謫罪人二千戍之，由是吐蕃不敢近青海。

translations.literal: Han judged its rivers and plains suitable for pasturage, sent two thousand exiled convicts to garrison it, and from this the Tibetans did not dare approach Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: Han found the rivers and plains there well suited to grazing, posted two thousand convicts in exile to garrison the place, and thereafter the Tibetans no longer dared come near Qinghai.

sentences.zh: 天寶八載，詔翰以朔方、河東群牧兵十萬攻吐蕃石堡城。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianbao, an edict ordered Han to take one hundred thousand herd-troop soldiers of Shuofang and Hedong to attack the Tibetan fortress of Shibao.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tianbao, the emperor ordered Han to lead one hundred thousand herd-troop soldiers from Shuofang and Hedong against the Tibetan stronghold of Shibao.

sentences.zh: 數日未克，翰怒，捽其將高秀岩、張守瑜，將斬之。

translations.literal: Several days passed without capture; Han in anger seized his generals Gao Xiuyan and Zhang Shouyu and was about to behead them.
translations.idiomatic: After several days the city had not fallen. Han in a fury seized his generals Gao Xiuyan and Zhang Shouyu and prepared to execute them.

sentences.zh: 秀岩請三日期，如期而下。

translations.literal: Xiuyan asked for three days' time and, on the appointed day, took the city.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyan begged for three days, and on the deadline the fortress fell.

sentences.zh: 遂以赤嶺為西塞，開屯田，備軍實。

translations.literal: He then made Chiling the western barrier, opened military colonies, and stocked provisions for the army.
translations.idiomatic: He then made Chiling the western frontier barrier, opened military colonies, and built up stores for the army.

sentences.zh: 加特進，賜賚彌渥。

translations.literal: He was given the special advancement rank, and imperial gifts grew ever more lavish.
translations.idiomatic: He received the rank of special advancement, and the emperor's gifts grew ever more generous.

sentences.zh: 十一載，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was further given the rank of Grand Preceptor with the same ceremonial privileges as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was further granted the rank of Grand Preceptor with ceremonial privileges equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 翰素與安祿山、安思順不平，帝每欲和解之。

translations.literal: Han had long been on bad terms with An Lushan and An Sishun; the emperor often wished to reconcile them.
translations.idiomatic: Han had long been at odds with An Lushan and An Sishun, and the emperor often tried to reconcile them.

sentences.zh: 會三人俱來朝，帝使驃騎大將軍高力士宴城東，翰等皆集。

translations.literal: When all three came to court together, the emperor had Flying-Cavalry Grand General Gao Lishi give a banquet east of the city; Han and the others all assembled.
translations.idiomatic: When all three arrived at court together, the emperor had Flying-Cavalry Grand General Gao Lishi host a banquet east of the city, and Han and the others all attended.

sentences.zh: 詔尚食生擊鹿，取血瀹腸為熱洛河以賜之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Imperial Kitchen to slaughter a deer alive, take its blood, and boil the intestines into a dish called "Hot River of Luo" to bestow on them.
translations.idiomatic: By edict the Imperial Kitchen slaughtered a deer alive, drew its blood, and boiled the intestines into a dish called Hot River of Luo, which was served to the guests.

sentences.zh: 翰母，于闐王女也。

translations.literal: Han's mother was a daughter of the king of Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: Han's mother was a daughter of the king of Khotan.

sentences.zh: 祿山謂翰曰：「我父胡，母突厥；

translations.literal: Lushan said to Han: "My father was a Hu and my mother a Turk;
translations.idiomatic: Lushan said to Han, "My father was a Hu and my mother a Turk;

sentences.zh: 公父突厥，母胡。

translations.literal: your father was a Turk and your mother a Hu.
translations.idiomatic: your father was a Turk and your mother a Hu.

sentences.zh: 族類本同，安得不親愛？

translations.literal: Our peoples are the same — how can we fail to be close?
translations.idiomatic: Our blood is the same — how can we not be kin?

sentences.zh: 」翰曰：「諺言'狐向窟嗥，不祥'，以忘本也。

translations.literal: " Han said: "A proverb says, 'When a fox howls toward its den, it is ill-omened' — it has forgotten its roots.
translations.idiomatic: " Han replied, "There is a saying: 'When a fox howls toward its burrow, it is an ill omen' — it means one has forgotten where he came from.

sentences.zh: 兄既見愛，敢不盡心。

translations.literal: Since you, elder brother, show me affection, how dare I not give you my whole heart?
translations.idiomatic: Since you show me affection, elder brother, how could I not serve you with all my heart?

sentences.zh: 」祿山以翰譏其胡，怒駡曰：「突厥敢爾！

translations.literal: " Lushan, because Han had mocked his Hu ancestry, cursed in anger: "You Turk — how dare you!
translations.idiomatic: " Lushan, stung by Han's jibe about his Hu blood, cursed in fury, "You Turk — how dare you!

sentences.zh: 」翰欲應之，力士目翰，翰托醉去。

translations.literal: " Han wished to answer back; Lishi signaled Han with his eyes; Han pleaded drunkenness and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " Han started to answer in kind, but Lishi caught his eye. Han pretended to be drunk and left.

sentences.zh: 久之，進封涼國公，兼河西節度使。

translations.literal: After some time he was advanced in rank and enfeoffed as Duke of Liang, and also made military commissioner of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was promoted and enfeoffed as Duke of Liang, and also appointed military commissioner of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 攻破吐蕃洪濟、大莫門等城，收黃河九曲，以其地置洮陽郡，築神策、宛秀二軍。

translations.literal: He broke through the Tibetan cities of Hongji and Damen and others, recovered the nine bends of the Yellow River, established Taoyang Commandery on that territory, and built the two armies of Shence and Wansiu.
translations.idiomatic: He captured the Tibetan cities of Hongji, Damen, and others, recovered the nine bends of the Yellow River, established Taoyang Commandery on the conquered land, and built the Shence and Wansiu garrisons.

sentences.zh: 進封西平郡王，賜音樂、田園，又賜一子五品官，裨將賞拜有差。

translations.literal: He was further enfeoffed as Prince of Xiping Commandery, granted music and estates, and one of his sons was given a fifth-rank office; his subordinate generals received rewards and appointments in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: He was further enfeoffed as Prince of Xiping Commandery and given musicians and estates; one of his sons received a fifth-rank post, and his subordinate generals were rewarded and promoted according to merit.

sentences.zh: 宰相楊國忠惡祿山，白髮其反狀，故厚結翰。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Yang Guozhong hated Lushan and reported to the emperor signs of his rebellion; therefore he cultivated a close bond with Han.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Yang Guozhong despised Lushan and had already warned the emperor of his rebellious intent, so he cultivated a close alliance with Han.

sentences.zh: 俄進太子少保。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 翰耆酒，極聲色，因風痹，體不仁。

translations.literal: Han was fond of wine and indulged to the utmost in music and women; because of wind paralysis his body lost sensation.
translations.idiomatic: Han was devoted to wine and pursued music and women to excess; rheumatism left his limbs numb and without feeling.

sentences.zh: 既疾廢，遂還京師，闔門不朝請。

translations.literal: Once disabled by illness, he returned to the capital and kept his household gates closed, not attending court.
translations.idiomatic: When illness left him incapacitated, he returned to the capital, shut his gates, and ceased attending court.

sentences.zh: 十四載，祿山反，封常清以王師敗。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Lushan rebelled, and Feng Changqing was defeated by the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Lushan rose in rebellion, and Feng Changqing was beaten by the imperial forces.

sentences.zh: 帝乃召見翰，拜太子先鋒兵馬元帥，以田良丘為軍司馬，蕭昕為判官，王思禮、鉗耳大福、李承光、高元蕩、蘇法鼎、管崇嗣為屬將，火拔歸仁、李武定、渾萼、契苾寧以本部隸麾下，凡河、隴、朔方、奴刺等十二部兵二十萬守潼關。

translations.literal: The emperor then summoned Han, appointed him Grand Marshal of the Heir Apparent's Vanguard Army, made Tian Liangqiu army secretary, Xiao Xin judge-advocate, Wang Sili, Qian'er Dafu, Li Chengguang, Gao Yuandang, Su Fading, and Guan Chongsi staff generals, and placed Huoba Guiren, Li Wuding, Hun'e, and Qibi Ning with their native troops under his command — in all two hundred thousand troops from twelve divisions including He, Long, Shuofang, and Nuci to hold Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then summoned Han, made him Grand Marshal of the Heir Apparent's Vanguard Army, appointed Tian Liangqiu army secretary and Xiao Xin judge-advocate, and named Wang Sili, Qian'er Dafu, Li Chengguang, Gao Yuandang, Su Fading, and Guan Chongsi as staff generals. Huoba Guiren, Li Wuding, Hun'e, and Qibi Ning brought their tribal contingents under his banner. In all, two hundred thousand men from twelve commands — He, Long, Shuofang, Nuci, and others — were to hold Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 師始東，先驅牙旗觸門，墮注旄，幹折，眾惡之。

translations.literal: When the army first marched east, the vanguard command pennant struck the gate, the tassel banner fell, the shaft broke, and the troops regarded it as ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: As the army first marched east, the vanguard's command pennant struck the gate, the tasseled banner fell, and the shaft snapped — an omen the troops took as evil.

sentences.zh: 天子禦勤政樓臨送，詔翰以軍行，過門毋下，百官郊餞，旌旗亙二百里。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven went to the Qinzheng Tower to see them off in person, ordered that Han need not dismount when passing through the gates on campaign, and officials of every rank saw them off beyond the suburbs; banners and flags stretched two hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself went to the Qinzheng Tower to see them off, decreed that Han need not dismount when the army passed through the gates, and the whole bureaucracy escorted them beyond the city. Banners and standards lined the road for two hundred li.

sentences.zh: 翰惶恐，數以疾自言，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Han was fearful and repeatedly pleaded illness, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Han was terrified and repeatedly pleaded his illness, but the emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 然病痼不能事，以軍政委良丘，使王思禮主騎，李承光主步。

translations.literal: Yet his chronic illness prevented him from commanding; he entrusted military affairs to Liangqiu, had Wang Sili command the cavalry, and Li Chengguang command the infantry.
translations.idiomatic: But his chronic illness left him unable to command. He delegated military affairs to Liangqiu, put Wang Sili in charge of the cavalry, and Li Chengguang in charge of the infantry.

sentences.zh: 三人爭長，政令無所統一，眾攜弛，無鬥意。

translations.literal: The three men vied for precedence; orders had no single authority; the troops grew lax and had no will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: The three men jockeyed for authority, orders went out from no single hand, the ranks grew slack, and the army lost its will to fight.

sentences.zh: 明年，進拜尚書左僕射、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and made a co-signer of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and made a co-signer of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 祿山遣子慶緒攻關，翰擊走之。

translations.literal: Lushan sent his son Qingxu to attack the pass; Han drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan sent his son Qingxu to assault the pass, and Han repulsed him.

sentences.zh: 始，安思順度祿山必反，嘗為帝言，得不坐。

translations.literal: At the beginning, An Sishun had judged that Lushan would certainly rebel and had once told the emperor; for this he escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, An Sishun had foreseen that Lushan would rebel and had warned the emperor, and for that he had escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 翰既惡祿山，又怨思順。

translations.literal: Han both hated Lushan and resented Sishun.
translations.idiomatic: Han hated Lushan and bore a grudge against Sishun as well.

sentences.zh: 及是，知重兵在己，有所論請，天子重違，因偽為賊書遺思順者，使關邏禽以獻。

translations.literal: At this time, knowing that the main army was in his hands and that whatever he requested the Son of Heaven would find hard to refuse, he forged a letter from the rebels to Sishun, had border patrols seize it and present it.
translations.idiomatic: Now, knowing the main army was his and that the emperor would hesitate to refuse his requests, he forged a rebel letter addressed to Sishun, had border patrols seize it, and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 翰因疏七罪，請誅之。

translations.literal: Han then memorialized listing seven crimes and asked that Sishun be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Han then submitted a memorial listing seven crimes and asking that Sishun be put to death.

sentences.zh: 有詔思順及弟元貞皆賜死，徙放其家。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that Sishun and his younger brother Yuanzhen both be granted death; their families were exiled.
translations.idiomatic: An edict condemned Sishun and his younger brother Yuanzhen to death and exiled their families.

sentences.zh: 國忠始懼。

translations.literal: Guozhong began to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong began to fear for himself.

sentences.zh: 或說翰曰：「祿山本以誅國忠故稱兵，今若留卒三萬守關，悉精銳度滻水誅君側，此漢挫七國計也。

translations.literal: Someone said to Han: "Lushan originally raised troops to execute Guozhong; if you now leave thirty thousand men to hold the pass and lead your picked troops across the Chan River to strike the emperor's side, this is the Han plan that broke the Seven Kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged Han, "Lushan took up arms chiefly to destroy Guozhong. Leave thirty thousand men to hold the pass, cross the Chan with your elite troops, and strike at the court itself — the same stratagem the Han used to crush the Seven Kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 」思禮亦勸翰。

translations.literal: " Sili also urged Han.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Sili urged the same course.

sentences.zh: 翰猶豫未發，謀頗露。

translations.literal: Han hesitated and did not act; the plot leaked out somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Han wavered and did not move, and word of the plan began to spread.

sentences.zh: 國忠大駭，入見帝曰：「兵法，安不忘危。

translations.literal: Guozhong was greatly alarmed, entered to see the emperor, and said: "In the art of war, one must not forget danger in times of peace.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong was terrified. He went before the emperor and said, "In the art of war, one must never forget danger even in security.

sentences.zh: 大兵在潼關而無後殿，萬有一不利，京師危矣。

translations.literal: The main army is at Tong Pass with no rear guard; if anything goes wrong, the capital will be in peril.
translations.idiomatic: The main force sits at Tong Pass with no reserve behind it. If anything goes wrong, the capital itself will be at risk.

sentences.zh: 」即募牧兒三千人，日夜訓練，以劍南列將分統之。

translations.literal: " He immediately recruited three thousand herdboys, trained them day and night, and had generals from Jiannan command them in turn.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately recruited three thousand herdboys, drilled them day and night, and put them under rotating command of generals from Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 又募萬人屯灞上，使腹心杜乾運為帥。

translations.literal: He also recruited ten thousand men and stationed them at Bashang, making his trusted follower Du Qianyun commander.
translations.idiomatic: He also raised ten thousand men and encamped them at Bashang under his trusted follower Du Qianyun.

sentences.zh: 翰疑圖己，表請乾運兵隸節下，因詭召乾運計事者，至軍，即斬首梟牙門，並其軍。

translations.literal: Han suspected a plot against himself, memorialized asking that Qianyun's troops be placed under his command, and under the pretext of summoning Qianyun to discuss affairs, beheaded him at the army gate and displayed his head, and absorbed his force.
translations.idiomatic: Han suspected a move against him, memorialized to have Qianyun's troops placed under his own command, then summoned Qianyun on a pretext, executed him at the army gate, displayed his head, and absorbed his command.

sentences.zh: 國忠愈恐，謂其子曰：「吾無死所矣！

translations.literal: Guozhong grew more fearful and said to his son: "I have no place left to die!
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong grew still more afraid and told his son, "There is nowhere left for me to die!

sentences.zh: 」然翰亦不自安，又謀久不決。

translations.literal: " Yet Han also was not at ease, and again deliberated without reaching a decision.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet Han too was ill at ease, and again he deliberated without deciding.

sentences.zh: 數奏言：「祿山雖竊據河朔，不得人心，請持重以敝之，待其離隙，可不血刃而禽。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized: "Although Lushan has seized Hebei, he has not won men's hearts; I ask that we hold firm and wear him down, wait for divisions to open among them, and then capture him without drawing a blade.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized, "Though Lushan holds Hebei, he has not won the people's hearts. Hold fast and wear him down; when cracks appear among them, we can take him without shedding blood.

sentences.zh: 」賊將崔乾祐守陝郡，僕旗鼓，羸師以誘戰。

translations.literal: " The rebel general Cui Qianyou held Shaan Commandery, lowered his banners and drums, and displayed a weak force to lure battle.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebel general Cui Qianyou held Shaan Commandery, furled his banners and drums, and paraded a feeble force to bait Han into battle.

sentences.zh: 覘者曰：「賊無備，可圖也。

translations.literal: Scouts said: "The rebels are unprepared — they can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Scouts reported, "The rebels are off guard — they can be struck.

sentences.zh: 」帝信之，詔翰進討。

translations.literal: " The emperor believed them and ordered Han to advance and attack.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor believed them and ordered Han to advance and attack.

sentences.zh: 翰報曰：「祿山慣用兵，今始為逆，不能無備，是陰計誘我。

translations.literal: Han replied: "Lushan is skilled in warfare; now that he has just turned rebel he cannot be without preparations — this is a hidden plan to lure us.
translations.idiomatic: Han replied, "Lushan is a seasoned commander. Having just rebelled, he cannot be unprepared — this is a trap laid to draw us out.

sentences.zh: 賊遠來，利在速戰。

translations.literal: The rebels have come from afar; their advantage lies in swift battle.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels have marched far; their advantage lies in forcing a quick fight.

sentences.zh: 王師堅守，毋輕出關，計之上也。

translations.literal: For the imperial army to hold firm and not lightly leave the pass is the best plan.
translations.idiomatic: The best course is for the imperial army to stand firm and not leave the pass lightly.

sentences.zh: 且四方兵未集，宜觀事勢，不必速。」

translations.literal: Moreover troops from the four quarters have not yet assembled; we should observe how matters develop and need not act in haste."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, troops from all quarters have not yet gathered. We should watch how matters unfold and need not hurry."

sentences.zh: 當是時，祿山雖盜河、洛，所過殘殺，人人怨之，淹時月不能進尺寸地。

translations.literal: At that time, although Lushan had seized the Yellow and Luo rivers, everywhere he passed he slaughtered and ravaged; everyone resented him, and after months he could not advance a single inch of ground.
translations.idiomatic: By then, though Lushan had overrun the Yellow and Luo valleys, his path was one of slaughter and ruin, and the people hated him. Months passed and he could not push forward another inch.

sentences.zh: 又郭子儀、李光弼兵益進，取常山十數郡。

translations.literal: Moreover the armies of Guo Ziyi and Li Guangbi pressed forward and recovered more than ten commanderies of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the armies of Guo Ziyi and Li Guangbi advanced and recaptured more than ten commanderies in Changshan.

sentences.zh: 祿山始悔反矣，將還幽州以自固。

translations.literal: Lushan began to regret the rebellion and intended to return to Youzhou to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan began to regret the rebellion and planned to withdraw to Youzhou and fortify himself there.

sentences.zh: 而國忠計迫，謬說帝趣翰出潼關復陝、洛。

translations.literal: But Guozhong, pressed by his own calculations, falsely persuaded the emperor to urge Han to leave Tong Pass and recover Shaan and Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: But Guozhong, driven by his own desperation, misled the emperor into pressing Han to leave Tong Pass and retake Shaan and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 時子儀、光弼遙計曰：「翰病且耄，賊素知之，諸軍烏合不足戰。

translations.literal: At that time Ziyi and Guangbi sent word from afar: "Han is ill and aged; the rebels have long known this; the various armies are a motley gathering and cannot fight.
translations.idiomatic: From afar Guo Ziyi and Li Guangbi counseled, "Han is sick and old, and the rebels know it well. These armies are a hurried assembly and cannot stand battle.

sentences.zh: 今賊悉銳兵南破宛、洛，而以餘眾守幽州，吾直搗之，覆其巢窟，質叛族以招逆徒，祿山之首可致。

translations.literal: Now the rebels have sent all their crack troops south to break Wan and Luoyang, while the remainder holds Youzhou; if we strike straight at them, overturn their nest, and hold their rebel kin hostage to summon the turncoats, Lushan's head can be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels have poured their best troops south against Wan and Luoyang while leaving the rest to hold Youzhou. If we strike directly at their base, overturn their nest, and hold their rebel families hostage to draw the turncoats back, Lushan's head can be taken.

sentences.zh: 若師出潼關，變生京師，天下怠矣。

translations.literal: If the army leaves Tong Pass, trouble will arise in the capital and the realm will slacken.
translations.idiomatic: If the army leaves Tong Pass, trouble will erupt at the capital and the whole empire will lose heart.

sentences.zh: 」乃極言請翰固關無出軍。

translations.literal: " They then spoke at length asking that Han hold the pass and not send out troops.
translations.idiomatic: " They pleaded at length that Han hold the pass and not march out.

sentences.zh: 而帝入國忠之言，使使者趣戰，項背相望也。

translations.literal: But the emperor followed Guozhong's words and sent messengers one after another to urge battle, their backs nearly touching as they came and went.
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor heeded Guozhong instead and sent messenger after messenger to demand battle, their trains passing back to back on the road.

sentences.zh: 翰窘不知所出。

translations.literal: Han, cornered, knew not what course to take.
translations.idiomatic: Han, trapped, no longer knew what to do.

sentences.zh: 六月，引而東，慟哭出關，次靈寶西原，與乾祐戰。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he led the army east, weeping as he left the pass, halted at the western plain of Lingbao, and fought Qianyou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he marched east, weeping as he passed through the gate, and encamped on the western plain of Lingbao to give battle to Cui Qianyou.

sentences.zh: 由關門七十里，道險隘，其南薄山，北阻河，賊以數千人先伏險。

translations.literal: Seventy li from Tong Gate the road was narrow and perilous, mountains pressing close on the south and the river blocking the north; the rebels had first placed several thousand men in ambush along the defile.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy li beyond the pass the road grew treacherous, mountains hemming it on the south and the river on the north. The rebels had already hidden several thousand men along the heights.

sentences.zh: 翰浮舟中流以觀軍，謂乾祐兵寡，易之，促士卒進，道岨無行列。

translations.literal: Han floated a boat midstream to observe the army, judged Qianyou's forces few and held them cheap, urged the soldiers forward; on the steep road there was no order of march.
translations.idiomatic: Han rode a boat into midstream to watch his troops, decided Qianyou's force was too small to matter, and pressed the men forward. On the steep track they lost all formation.

sentences.zh: 賊乘高頹石下擊，殺士甚眾。

translations.literal: The rebels rolled stones down from the heights and killed many soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels hurled stones down from above and slaughtered a great many men.

sentences.zh: 翰與良丘登北阜，以軍三萬夾河鳴鼓，思禮等以精卒居前，餘軍十萬次之。

translations.literal: Han and Liangqiu climbed the northern rise; thirty thousand troops beat drums on both sides of the river; Sili and others led picked troops in front, the remaining hundred thousand followed.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Tian Liangqiu took a hill north of the river and set thirty thousand men drumming on both banks. Wang Sili and the other captains led the elite vanguard; the remaining hundred thousand filed in behind.

sentences.zh: 乾祐為陣，十十五五，或卻或進，而陌刀五千列陣後。

translations.literal: Qianyou formed his battle line in scattered groups of tens and fives, now retreating, now advancing, while five thousand wielders of the mo dao stood in ranks behind.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyou drew up his line in loose clusters of ten and five, feinting retreat and advance, while five thousand men with mo dao blades massed behind the front.

sentences.zh: 王師視其陣無法，指觀嗤笑，曰：「禽賊乃會食。」

translations.literal: The imperial army, seeing his formation disordered, pointed and laughed, saying: "We will have our meal after we capture the rebels."
translations.idiomatic: The imperial troops, seeing this ragged array, pointed and jeered, "We'll eat once we've bagged the rebels."

sentences.zh: 及戰，乾祐旗少偃，如欲遁者，王師懈，不為備。

translations.literal: When battle joined, Qianyou's banners dipped slightly as though he meant to flee; the imperial army relaxed and took no precautions.
translations.idiomatic: Once the fight began, Qianyou's banners dipped as if he meant to run. The imperial army slackened and dropped its guard.

sentences.zh: 伏忽起薄戰，皆奮死鬥。

translations.literal: Ambush troops suddenly rose and pressed the fight; all fought desperately to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden troops sprang up and closed in; every man fought as if ready to die.

sentences.zh: 翰以氈蒙馬車，畫龍虎，飾金銀爪目，將駭賊，掎戈矢逐北。

translations.literal: Han covered ox carts with felt, painted dragons and tigers on them, adorned them with gold and silver claws and eyes, intending to terrify the rebels, and pressed the pursuit with spears and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Han draped ox carts in felt, painted them with dragons and tigers, and fitted them with gilded claws and eyes to frighten the enemy, then drove forward with spears and arrows in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 賊負薪塞路，順風火其車，熛焱熾突，騰煙如夜，士不復相辨，自相鬥殺，屍血狼籍，久乃悟。

translations.literal: The rebels carried firewood to block the road, set the carts afire with the wind at their backs; flames leaped and smoke rose dark as night; soldiers could no longer tell friend from foe and killed one another; corpses and blood lay everywhere; only after long did they realize.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels piled brush to choke the road and, with the wind at their backs, torched the carts. Fire leaped up and smoke blotted out the day like night. Men could no longer tell friend from foe and turned on one another; bodies and blood covered the ground before they understood what had happened.

sentences.zh: 又棄甲奔山谷及陷河死者十一二。

translations.literal: Again those who cast off armor and fled into valleys or drowned in the river numbered one or two in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Another tenth or so threw off their armor, fled into the ravines, or drowned in the river.

sentences.zh: 有糧艘百餘，軍爭濟，艘輒沉，至縛矛盾乘以度，喧叫振天地。

translations.literal: There were more than a hundred grain boats; the army scrambled to cross, boats sank at once; men bound spears and shields together to raft across; shouts shook heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred grain boats stood ready. Soldiers fought to board them; each boat sank under the crush. Men lashed spears and shields together to raft across, their cries shaking heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 賊乘之，奔潰略盡。

translations.literal: The rebels seized the moment and the rout was nearly complete.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pressed the advantage, and the army broke almost to the last man.

sentences.zh: 始，斗門有三塹，廣二丈，深一丈，士馬奔籥相壓迮，少選塹平，後至者踐之以入。

translations.literal: At first there were three trenches at Dou Gate, twenty feet wide and ten deep; men and horses crushed together in the rush; in a little while the trenches were filled level; those coming after trampled over them to enter.
translations.idiomatic: At Dou Gate three trenches, each twenty feet wide and ten deep, had been dug. Horses and men piled into them in the stampede; within moments the ditches were filled flat, and those behind trampled over the dead to get through.

sentences.zh: 既敗，翰引數百騎絕河還營，羸兵裁八千，至潼津，收散卒復守關。

translations.literal: After the defeat Han led several hundred horsemen across the river back to camp; his exhausted troops numbered only eight thousand; reaching Tong Ford he gathered scattered soldiers and again held the pass.
translations.idiomatic: After the rout Han crossed the river with a few hundred riders and regrouped. Barely eight thousand weary soldiers remained. At Tong Ford he rallied the stragglers and once more manned the pass.

sentences.zh: 乾祐進攻，於是火拔歸仁等紿翰出關，翰曰：「何邪？

translations.literal: Qianyou pressed the attack; then Huoba Guiren and others deceived Han into leaving the pass. Han said: "What is this?
translations.idiomatic: When Qianyou attacked again, Huoba Guiren and others tricked Han into abandoning the pass. Han asked, "What is this?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「公以二十萬眾，一日覆沒，持是安歸？

translations.literal: " They said: "With your two hundred thousand men destroyed in a single day, where can you go now?
translations.idiomatic: " They said, "You led two hundred thousand men and lost them in one day. Where can you turn now?

sentences.zh: 公不見高仙芝等事乎？

translations.literal: Have you not seen what happened to Gao Xianzhi and the others?
translations.idiomatic: Have you forgotten what befell Gao Xianzhi and the others?

sentences.zh: 」翰曰：「吾寧效仙芝死，汝舍我。

translations.literal: " Han said: "I would rather die like Xianzhi — leave me.
translations.idiomatic: " Han said, "I would rather die as Xianzhi did. Leave me.

sentences.zh: 」歸仁不從，執以降賊，械送洛陽，京師震動，由是天子西幸。

translations.literal: " Guiren would not listen, seized him and surrendered to the rebels, sent him in shackles to Luoyang; the capital trembled; hence the Son of Heaven fled west.
translations.idiomatic: " Guiren refused. He seized Han, surrendered him to the rebels, and sent him in chains to Luoyang. The capital shook with fear, and the emperor fled west.

sentences.zh: 祿山見翰責曰：「汝常易我，今何如？

translations.literal: Lushan saw Han and rebuked him: "You always looked down on me — how about now?
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan saw Han he taunted him: "You always despised me — what do you say now?

sentences.zh: 」翰俯伏謝罪曰：「陛下撥亂主。

translations.literal: " Han prostrated himself and apologized: "Your Majesty is the lord who will quell disorder.
translations.idiomatic: " Han kowtowed and pleaded, "Your Majesty is the sovereign who will restore order to the realm.

sentences.zh: 今天下未平，李光弼在土門，來瑱在河南，魯炅在南陽，臣為陛下以尺書招之，三面可平。

translations.literal: The realm is not yet at peace. Li Guangbi is at Tumen, Lai Tian in Henan, Lu Kui at Nanyang — I will summon them for Your Majesty with a brief letter, and three sides can be pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The empire is not yet settled. Li Guangbi holds Tumen, Lai Tian is in Henan, and Lu Kui at Nanyang. Let me summon them with a single letter, and three fronts can be pacified at once.

sentences.zh: 」祿山悅，即署司空、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: " Lushan was pleased and immediately appointed him Minister of Works and co-signer of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: " Lushan was delighted and at once made him Minister of Works and co-signer of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 執火拔歸仁，曰：「背主忘義，吾不爾容。

translations.literal: He seized Huoba Guiren and said: "You betrayed your lord and forgot righteousness — I will not spare you.
translations.idiomatic: He then seized Huoba Guiren and said, "You betrayed your master and forgot your duty — I will not pardon you.

sentences.zh: 」斬之。

translations.literal: " He beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: " And had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 翰以書招諸將，諸將皆讓翰不死節。

translations.literal: Han sent letters summoning the generals; all reproached Han for not dying with honor.
translations.idiomatic: Han wrote to the generals urging them to submit, but every one rebuked him for failing to die with honor.

sentences.zh: 祿山知事不可就，囚之。

translations.literal: Lushan knew the scheme would not succeed and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan saw the plan would not work and had him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 東京平，安慶緒以翰度河。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital was pacified, An Qingxu had Han cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Capital was retaken, An Qingxu had Han brought across the river.

sentences.zh: 及敗，乃殺之。

translations.literal: When Qingxu was defeated, he killed Han.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingxu in turn was defeated, he had Han executed.

sentences.zh: 翰為人嚴，少恩。

translations.literal: Han was strict as a man and sparing in kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Han was a stern man and showed little mercy.

sentences.zh: 軍行未嘗恤士饑寒，有啗民椹者，痛笞辱之。

translations.literal: On campaign he never showed concern for soldiers' hunger or cold; those who ate mulberries from the people were beaten and humiliated.
translations.idiomatic: On the march he never troubled himself over hunger or cold among the ranks. Any soldier caught eating mulberries from the countryside was flogged and shamed.

sentences.zh: 監軍李大宜在軍中，不治事，與將士樗蒱、飲酒、彈箜篌琵琶為樂，而士米籺不饜。

translations.literal: Military overseer Li Dayi was in the army, attending to no affairs, gambling, drinking, and playing konghou and pipa with the officers for amusement, while the soldiers' grain rations left them unsatisfied.
translations.idiomatic: The army overseer Li Dayi ignored his duties and spent his days gambling, drinking, and playing the konghou and pipa with the officers, while the men went hungry on short rations.

sentences.zh: 帝令中人袁思藝勞師，士皆訴衣服穿空，帝即斥禦服餘者，制袍十萬以賜其軍，翰藏庫中，及敗，封鐍如故。

translations.literal: The emperor sent eunuch Yuan Siyi to comfort the army; the soldiers all complained their clothes were worn through; the emperor immediately rebuked him and had one hundred thousand robes made from surplus imperial dress to gift the army; Han stored them in the warehouse, and at defeat the seals remained unbroken as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the eunuch Yuan Siyi to comfort the troops. The men complained their clothes were in tatters. The emperor at once stripped surplus robes from the palace stores and had one hundred thousand new coats made for the army. Han locked them in the depot; when he was defeated the seals had never been broken.

sentences.zh: 先是，有客梁慎初遺翰書，請壁勿戰以屈賊，翰善之，奏為左武衛胄曹參軍，留幕府。

translations.literal: Earlier a guest, Liang Shenchu, had sent Han a letter advising him to hold the wall and not fight in order to wear down the rebels; Han approved and memorialized to appoint him Left Martial Guard armor-and-weapons adjutant, kept in the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a visitor named Liang Shenchu had written urging Han to stand on the defensive and wear the rebels down rather than give battle. Han approved the advice, memorialized to appoint him adjutant of armor and weapons in the Left Martial Guard, and kept him on staff.

sentences.zh: 及翰與國忠貳，慎初曰：「難將作矣。

translations.literal: When Han turned against Guozhong, Shenchu said: "Disaster is about to happen.
translations.idiomatic: When Han fell out with Guozhong, Shenchu said, "Trouble is coming.

sentences.zh: 」乃遁去。

translations.literal: " Then he fled away.
translations.idiomatic: " And slipped away.

sentences.zh: 翰失守，華陰、馮翊、上洛郡官吏皆潰。

translations.literal: After Han lost the pass, officials of Huayin, Tongzhou, and Shangluo commands all collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: After Han lost the pass, the civil officials of Huayin, Tongzhou, and Shangluo all fled or surrendered.

sentences.zh: 帝遣劍南將劉光庭等將新募兵萬餘人往助翰，未至而翰被縛雲。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Jiannan general Liu Guangting and others with more than ten thousand newly recruited troops to aid Han; before they arrived Han had already been captured.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Liu Guangting of Jiannan and others with more than ten thousand freshly levied troops to reinforce Han, but before they arrived Han had already been taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 其後贈太尉，諡曰武湣。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously given Grand Marshal and the posthumous title Wumin.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was posthumously made Grand Marshal and given the posthumous title Wumin.

sentences.zh: 子 曜

translations.literal: Son Yao
translations.idiomatic: His Son Yao

sentences.zh: 子曜，字子明。

translations.literal: His son Yao, courtesy name Ziming.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yao, courtesy name Ziming.

sentences.zh: 八歲，玄宗召見華清宮，擢尚輦奉禦。

translations.literal: At eight years of age the emperor summoned him to Huaqing Palace and promoted him to Imperial Carriage Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he was summoned to Huaqing Palace by Emperor Xuanzong and appointed Imperial Carriage Attendant.

sentences.zh: 累遷光祿卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Minister of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Minister of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 以翰陷賊，哀憤號慟，故吏裴冕、杜鴻漸等見之歎息。

translations.literal: Because Han had fallen to the rebels, Yao wailed in grief and indignation; former subordinates Pei Mian and Du Hongjian sighed when they saw him.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell into rebel hands, Yao wailed in grief and rage. Former officers such as Pei Mian and Du Hongjian sighed at the sight of him.

sentences.zh: 李光弼討河北，曜請行，拜鴻臚卿，為光弼副。

translations.literal: When Li Guangbi campaigned in Hebei, Yao asked to go; he was appointed Minister of Ceremonial and Guangbi's deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Guangbi marched into Hebei, Yao asked to join the campaign and was made Minister of Ceremonial and Guangbi's deputy.

sentences.zh: 降安太清、救宋州有功，改殿中監，襲封，為東都鎮守兵馬使。

translations.literal: For subduing An Taiqing and relieving Songzhou he was rewarded, changed to Director of the Palace Directorate, inherited the enfeoffment, and became commissioner of the eastern capital garrison army and cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: For accepting the surrender of An Taiqing and relieving Songzhou he was rewarded, appointed Director of the Palace Directorate, inherited his father's title, and became commissioner of the eastern capital garrison and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 德宗立，召為左龍武大將軍。

translations.literal: When Dezong ascended, Yao was summoned as Left Dragon Martial Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong took the throne, Yao was recalled as Left Dragon Martial Grand General.

sentences.zh: 李希烈陷汝州，以周晃為偽刺史。

translations.literal: When Li Xilie captured Ruzhou, he installed Zhou Huang as false governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie seized Ruzhou, he installed Zhou Huang as puppet governor.

sentences.zh: 詔拜曜東都、汝州行營節度使，將鳳翔、邠甯、涇原、奉天、好畦兵萬人討希烈。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Yao military commissioner of the eastern capital and Ruzhou mobile camp, leading ten thousand troops from Fengxiang, Binning, Jingyuan, Fengtian, and Haoqi to campaign against Xilie.
translations.idiomatic: By edict Yao was made military commissioner of the eastern capital and Ruzhou field headquarters, commanding ten thousand men from Fengxiang, Binning, Jingyuan, Fengtian, and Haoqi against Li Xilie.

sentences.zh: 帝召見，問曰：「卿治兵孰與父賢？

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him and asked: "How does your command of troops compare with your father's excellence?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received him and asked, "How does your skill at leading troops compare with your father's?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「先臣，安敢比。

translations.literal: " He replied: "My late father — how dare I compare?
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "My late father — how dare I measure myself against him?

sentences.zh: 但斬長蛇，殪封豕，然後待罪私室，臣之願也。

translations.literal: But to behead the long snake and slay the penned pig, then await punishment in my private chamber — that is my wish.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if I can cut down this great serpent and slaughter this penned boar, then accept judgment at home — that is all I ask.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「爾父在開元時，朝廷無西憂；

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Your father in the Kaiyuan era — the court had no western worries;
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "In the Kaiyuan era your father left the court free of worry in the west;

sentences.zh: 今朕得卿，亦不東慮。

translations.literal: now that I have you, I have no eastern worries either.
translations.idiomatic: now that I have you, I need not fear trouble in the east either.

sentences.zh: 」及行，帝祖通化門。

translations.literal: " When he marched the emperor performed the farewell rite at Tonghua Gate.
translations.idiomatic: " As he set out, the emperor saw him off with rites at Tonghua Gate.

sentences.zh: 是日，牙幹折。

translations.literal: That day the command-staff shaft broke.
translations.idiomatic: That day the shaft of his command staff snapped.

sentences.zh: 時以翰出師已如此，而斬持旗者，卒以敗，今曜復爾，人憂之。

translations.literal: People recalled that when Han marched out it had been the same, and they executed the flag-bearer, yet he was defeated in the end; now Yao again — people feared for him.
translations.idiomatic: Men remembered that when Han had marched out something similar had happened — they had even executed the standard-bearer, yet Han was still destroyed. Now the same omen fell on Yao, and people feared for him.

sentences.zh: 曜擊賊，收汝州，禽晃以獻，斬其將二人。

translations.literal: Yao struck the rebels, recovered Ruzhou, captured Huang and presented him, and beheaded two enemy generals.
translations.idiomatic: Yao attacked the rebels, retook Ruzhou, captured Zhou Huang and sent him to the throne, and beheaded two enemy officers.

sentences.zh: 希烈退保許州。

translations.literal: Xilie withdrew to hold Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie fell back to defend Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔城襄城，曜以疲人版築不如按甲持重以挫之，帝不許。

translations.literal: An edict ordered fortifications built at Xiangcheng; Yao said that with exhausted men, building walls was inferior to holding armor and standing firm to wear the enemy down; the emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered walls raised at Xiangcheng. Yao argued that with worn-out troops it was better to hold position and grind the enemy down than to build ramparts. The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 有詔督戰。

translations.literal: There was an edict to press the battle.
translations.idiomatic: An edict came ordering him to attack at once.

sentences.zh: 曜進次潁橋，雷震軍中七馬斃，曜懼，還屯襄城。

translations.literal: Yao advanced to Ying Bridge; thunder killed seven horses in the army; Yao was afraid and withdrew to encamp at Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yao advanced to Ying Bridge. Lightning killed seven horses in the camp. Alarmed, he pulled back and encamped at Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 希烈遣眾萬人縱火攻柵，殪人于塹以薄壘，曜苦戰破之。

translations.literal: Xilie sent ten thousand men to set fire and attack the palisade, piled corpses in the moat to press the ramparts; Yao fought bitterly and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie sent ten thousand men to fire the stockade and fill the ditch with corpses to storm the walls. Yao fought them off at heavy cost.

sentences.zh: 居數月，希烈自率兵三萬圍曜，築甬道屬城，矢集如雨。

translations.literal: After several months Xilie personally led thirty thousand to besiege Yao, built covered ways connecting to the city, and arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Months later Xilie himself brought thirty thousand men to besiege Yao, built covered approaches to the walls, and rained arrows on the city.

sentences.zh: 帝遣神策將劉德信以兵三千援之，又詔河南都統李勉出兵相掎角。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Shence general Liu Dexin with three thousand troops to aid him, and also ordered Henan overall commander Li Mian to send troops in pincer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Liu Dexin of the Shence Army with three thousand men to relieve him and ordered Li Mian, overall commander of Henan, to strike in concert.

sentences.zh: 勉以「希烈在外，許守兵少，乘虛襲之，希烈自解」，乃遣部將與德信趨許，未至，有詔切讓，使班師。

translations.literal: Mian said that with Xilie outside and few defenders at Xu, if they struck the empty city Xilie would withdraw of himself; he sent a subordinate with Dexin toward Xu; before they arrived, an edict sharply rebuked them and ordered withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mian reasoned that with Xilie away from Xu the garrison was thin and a raid on the city would force him to lift the siege. He sent a subordinate with Dexin toward Xu, but before they arrived an angry edict recalled them.

sentences.zh: 德信等惶惑還，軍無斥候，至扈澗，為賊設伏詭擊，死者殆半，器械輜重皆亡。

translations.literal: Dexin and the others returned in confusion without scouts; at Hujian they were ambushed and deceptively struck; nearly half died; weapons and baggage were all lost.
translations.idiomatic: Dexin and his men retreated in disorder without scouts. At Hujian they walked into an ambush; nearly half were killed and all their arms and baggage were lost.

sentences.zh: 德信走汝州。

translations.literal: Dexin fled to Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dexin fled back to Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 勉恐東都危，使將李堅華以兵四千往守，賊梗道，不得入。

translations.literal: Mian feared the eastern capital was in danger and sent general Li Jianhua with four thousand men to hold it; rebels blocked the road and they could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for the eastern capital, Li Mian sent Li Jianhua with four thousand men to defend it, but the rebels blocked the roads and they never got through.

sentences.zh: 汴兵沮，襄城圍益急。

translations.literal: Bian troops were discouraged and the siege of Xiangcheng grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Morale among the Bian troops collapsed, and the siege of Xiangcheng tightened.

sentences.zh: 帝乃詔普王以荊、襄、江西、鄂、沔之師討蔡州，詔涇原節度使姚令言救襄城。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Prince Pu with armies from Jing, Xiang, Jiangxi, E, and Mian to campaign against Caizhou, and ordered Jingyuan military commissioner Yao Lingyan to rescue Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Prince Pu to march against Caizhou with forces from Jing, Xiang, Jiangxi, E, and Mian, and commanded Yao Lingyan, military commissioner of Jingyuan, to relieve Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 未行，京師亂，帝幸奉天。

translations.literal: Before they marched, the capital fell into disorder and the emperor fled to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Before they could move, the capital erupted in chaos and the emperor fled to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 襄城陷，曜走洛陽。

translations.literal: Xiangcheng fell; Yao fled to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangcheng fell. Yao escaped to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 會母喪，奪為東都畿、汝節度使。

translations.literal: Meeting his mother's mourning, mourning was set aside and he was made military commissioner of eastern capital Ji and Ru.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he was recalled from mourning and appointed military commissioner of the eastern capital Ji and Ru circuits.

sentences.zh: 遷河南尹。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Henan Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 曜拙於統禦，而銳殺戮，士畏而不懷。

translations.literal: Yao was clumsy at control but sharp in killing; soldiers feared but did not attach to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao was a poor commander but quick with the sword. His men feared him but gave him no loyalty.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，部將叛，夜焚河南門，曜挺身免。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan, subordinates rebelled and burned the Henan gate by night; Yao escaped bodily.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenyuan his officers mutinied and set fire to the Henan gate by night. Yao barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 帝以汴州刺史薛玨代之，召入為鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: The emperor replaced him with Bian prefect Xue Jue and summoned him as Minister of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replaced him with Xue Jue, prefect of Bian, and recalled Yao as Minister of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 終右驍衛上將軍，贈幽州大都督。

translations.literal: He ended as Right Xiaoqi Grand General and was posthumously given Metropolitan Prefect of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Right Xiaoqi Grand General and was posthumously made Metropolitan Prefect of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 子七人，俱以儒聞。

translations.literal: He had seven sons, all famed for scholarship.
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons, all noted for learning.

sentences.zh: 峘，茂才高第，有節概。

translations.literal: Han, distinguished in the maocai high examination, had integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Han passed the maocai examination with highest honors and was a man of principle.

sentences.zh: 崿、嵫、屺皆明經擢第。

translations.literal: E, Zi, and Qi all passed the classics examination.
translations.idiomatic: E, Zi, and Qi all earned their degrees in the classics examination.

sentences.zh: 高仙芝

translations.literal: Gao Xianzhi
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xianzhi

sentences.zh: 高仙芝，高麗人。

translations.literal: Gao Xianzhi, a man of Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xianzhi was a man of Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 父舍雞，初以將軍隸河西軍，為四鎮校將。

translations.literal: His father Sheji, at first a general attached to the Hexi Army, was a commandant of the Four Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sheji had first served as a general in the Hexi Army and became a commandant of the Four Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 仙芝年二十餘，從至安西，以父功補遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: Xianzhi in his twenties followed him to Anxi and through his father's merit was appointed mobile corps general.
translations.idiomatic: In his twenties Xianzhi followed him to Anxi and, through his father's service, was appointed a mobile corps general.

sentences.zh: 數年，父子並班。

translations.literal: After several years, father and son both served in the same ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years father and son were serving side by side in the same ranks.

sentences.zh: 仙芝美姿質，善騎射，父猶以其儒緩憂之。

translations.literal: Xianzhi had fine looks and was skilled at horse archery; his father still worried he was too soft and slow.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi was handsome and a fine mounted archer, yet his father still fretted that he was too gentle and unhurried.

sentences.zh: 初事節度使田仁琬、蓋嘉運等，不甚知名。

translations.literal: At first he served military commissioners Tian Renwan, Gai Jiayun, and others, not very well known.
translations.idiomatic: He first served under military commissioners Tian Renwan and Gai Jiayun and attracted little notice.

sentences.zh: 後事夫蒙靈察，乃善遇之。

translations.literal: Later he served Fumeng Lingcha and was then well treated.
translations.idiomatic: Later he entered the service of Fumeng Lingcha, who treated him with favor.

sentences.zh: 開元末，表為安西副都護、四鎮都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaiyuan era he was memorialized as deputy protector of Anxi and commandant of troops and horses of the Four Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kaiyuan era he was recommended as deputy protector of Anxi and commander of the Four Garrisons' troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 小勃律，其王為吐蕃所誘，妻以女，故西北二十餘國皆羈屬吐蕃。

translations.literal: Lesser Bolü — its king was enticed by the Tibetans, given a daughter in marriage, so more than twenty states northwest all became Tibetan dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: In Lesser Bolü the king had been won over by the Tibetans and given a princess in marriage, and more than twenty kingdoms to the northwest had fallen under Tibetan sway.

sentences.zh: 自仁琬以來三討之，皆無功。

translations.literal: Since Renwan three campaigns had been launched, all without success.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tian Renwan's time three expeditions had been sent against it, all failures.

sentences.zh: 天寶六載，詔仙芝以步騎一萬出討。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianbao an edict ordered Xianzhi with ten thousand infantry and cavalry to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianbao the emperor ordered Xianzhi to take ten thousand foot and horse soldiers on campaign.

sentences.zh: 是時步兵皆有私馬自隨，仙芝乃自安西過撥換城，入握瑟德，經疏勒，登蔥嶺，涉播密川，遂頓特勒滿川，行凡百日。

translations.literal: At that time every infantryman had a private horse; Xianzhi went from Anxi through Baohuan city, entered Wosede, via Kashgar, ascended the Pamirs, crossed the Bodai River, and halted at the Teller Man River — the march totaled one hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: Every infantryman then rode a private mount. Xianzhi marched from Anxi through Baohuan, entered Wosede, passed Kashgar, crossed the Pamirs, forded the Bodai River, and halted at the Teller Man River — a journey of one hundred days.

sentences.zh: 特勒滿川，即五識匿國也。

translations.literal: The Teller Man River is the land of the Five Shibei states.
translations.idiomatic: The Teller Man River lay in the territory of the Five Shibei kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 仙芝乃分軍為三，使疏勒趙崇玼自北穀道、撥換賈崇瓘祐自赤佛道、仙芝與監軍邊令誠自護蜜俱入，約會連雲堡。

translations.literal: Xianzhi then divided the army in three: he had Kashgar's Zhao Chongbi enter by the northern valley route, Baohuan's Jia Chongyun by the Chifo route, and Xianzhi with army overseer Bian Lingcheng by Humili — all to meet at Lianyun Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi split his force three ways: Zhao Chongbi of Kashgar by the northern valley, Jia Chongyun of Baohuan by the Chifo road, and Xianzhi himself with the army overseer Bian Lingcheng through Humili, all to rendezvous at Lianyun Fort.

sentences.zh: 堡有兵千餘。

translations.literal: The fort had more than a thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The fort held a garrison of more than a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 城南因山為柵，兵九千守之。

translations.literal: South of the city they used the mountain to build a palisade; nine thousand troops guarded it.
translations.idiomatic: South of the fort they built a stockade along the mountain slope, garrisoned by nine thousand men.

sentences.zh: 城下據婆勒川。

translations.literal: Below the city lay the Bole River.
translations.idiomatic: The city stood above the Bole River.

sentences.zh: 會川漲，不得度，仙芝殺牲祭川，命士人齎三日備集水涯，士不甚信。

translations.literal: The river happened to be in flood and could not be crossed; Xianzhi sacrificed animals to propitiate the river, ordered the men to carry three days' supplies and assemble on the bank; the soldiers did not much believe.
translations.idiomatic: The river was in spate and impassable. Xianzhi offered sacrifice to the stream and ordered the men to bring three days' rations to the bank. The troops were skeptical.

sentences.zh: 既涉，旗不沾，韉不濡。

translations.literal: Once they had crossed, flags were not wet, saddles were not soaked.
translations.idiomatic: When they forded it, their banners stayed dry and their saddles untouched by water.

sentences.zh: 兵已成列，仙芝喜，告令誠曰：「向吾方涉，賊擊我，我無類矣。

translations.literal: The troops were already in formation; Xianzhi was pleased and told Lingcheng: "Just now, as I was crossing, if the enemy had struck me, I would have been wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: With the army formed up, Xianzhi rejoiced and told Lingcheng, "A moment ago, while we were crossing, if the enemy had hit us we would have been destroyed.

sentences.zh: 今既濟而陣，天以賊賜我也。

translations.literal: Now that we have crossed and drawn up in battle array, Heaven has given the enemy to me.
translations.idiomatic: Now that we are across and in line of battle, Heaven has delivered the enemy into our hands.

sentences.zh: 」遂登山挑戰，日未中，破之。

translations.literal: " He then climbed the mountain to offer battle; before noon he broke them.
translations.idiomatic: " He then led the climb to give battle and routed them before noon.

sentences.zh: 拔其城，斬五千級，生禽千人，馬千餘匹，衣資器甲數萬計。

translations.literal: He took the city, beheaded five thousand, captured a thousand alive, more than a thousand horses, and tens of thousands of clothing, supplies, weapons, and armor.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed the city, killed five thousand, took a thousand prisoners, seized more than a thousand horses, and countless garments, stores, arms, and armor.

sentences.zh: 仙芝欲遂深入，令誠懼，不肯行。

translations.literal: Xianzhi wished to press deeper; Lingcheng was afraid and refused to go.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi wanted to push deeper inland, but Lingcheng was afraid and would not advance.

sentences.zh: 仙芝留羸弱三千使守，遂引師行。

translations.literal: Xianzhi left three thousand weak troops to hold the place and then led the army onward.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi left three thousand sick and weak men to hold the post and marched on.

sentences.zh: 三日，過坦駒嶺，嶺峻絕，下四十里。

translations.literal: After three days they crossed Tanju Ridge; the ridge was steep and sheer, with a descent of forty li.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later they crossed Tanju Ridge, a sheer drop of forty li.

sentences.zh: 仙芝恐士憚險不敢進，乃潛遣二十騎，衣阿弩越胡服來迎，先語部校曰：「阿弩越胡來迎，我無慮矣。

translations.literal: Xianzhi feared the men would dread the peril and not advance; he secretly sent twenty horsemen dressed in Annuoyue Hu garb to come welcome them, and first told the unit commanders: "The Annuoyue Hu have come to welcome us — I have no further worries.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing his men would balk at the drop, Xianzhi secretly sent twenty riders in Annuoyue dress to play envoys and told the officers beforehand, "The Annuoyue have come to meet us — we are safe.

sentences.zh: 」既至，士不肯下，曰：「公驅我何去？

translations.literal: " When they arrived, the soldiers would not descend, saying: "Where are you driving us?
translations.idiomatic: " When the army reached the ridge the men refused to go down. "Where are you leading us?" they cried.

sentences.zh: 」會二十人至，曰：「阿努越胡來迎，已數娑夷橋矣。

translations.literal: " Just then the twenty men arrived and said: "The Annuoyue Hu have come to welcome us — we have already counted off the Suoyi Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: " Then the twenty riders appeared and announced, "The Annuoyue envoys are here — we have already crossed the Suoyi Bridge several times.

sentences.zh: 」仙芝即陽喜，令士盡下。

translations.literal: " Xianzhi at once feigned delight and ordered the men all to descend.
translations.idiomatic: " Xianzhi pretended delight and ordered the whole army down the slope.

sentences.zh: 娑夷河，弱水也。

translations.literal: The Suoyi River is the Weak Water.
translations.idiomatic: The Suoyi River is the Weak Water.

sentences.zh: 既行三日，越胡來迎。

translations.literal: After marching three days, the Yue Hu came to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Three days on, the Yue tribes came out to meet them.

sentences.zh: 明日，至阿弩越城。

translations.literal: The next day they reached Annuoyue city.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they reached the city of Annuoyue.

sentences.zh: 遣將軍席元慶以精騎一千先往，謂小勃律王曰：「不窺若城，吾假道趨大勃律耳。

translations.literal: He sent General Xi Yuanqing with a thousand picked horsemen ahead, saying to the king of Lesser Bolü: "I am not spying on your city — I am merely passing through toward Greater Bolü.
translations.idiomatic: He sent General Xi Yuanqing ahead with a thousand elite horsemen to tell the king of Lesser Bolü, "We do not mean to inspect your city — we only ask passage toward Greater Bolü.

sentences.zh: 」城中大酋領皆吐蕃腹心，仙芝密令元慶曰：「若酋領逃者，弟出詔書呼之，賜以繒彩，至，皆縛以待我。

translations.literal: " The great chieftains in the city were all Tibetan confidants; Xianzhi secretly ordered Yuanqing: "If any chieftain flees, you produce an edict summoning him, bestow silk, and when he arrives bind them all to await me.
translations.idiomatic: " The leading chiefs in the city were Tibetan loyalists. Xianzhi secretly told Yuanqing, "If any chief tries to flee, produce an imperial summons, offer him silk, and when he comes bind him and hold him for me.

translations.literal: (The secret order continues.)
translations.idiomatic: (The secret order continues.)

sentences.zh: 」元慶如言。

translations.literal: " Yuanqing did as instructed.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuanqing did exactly as he was told.

sentences.zh: 仙芝至，悉斬之。

translations.literal: When Xianzhi arrived, he beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzhi arrived, he executed them all.

sentences.zh: 王及妻逃山穴，不可得，仙芝招喻，乃出降，因平其國。

translations.literal: The king and his wife fled into a mountain cave and could not be found; Xianzhi summoned and persuaded them, and they came out to surrender; he thereby pacified the state.
translations.idiomatic: The king and queen hid in a mountain cave and could not be reached. Xianzhi won them over with promises, and they surrendered, completing the conquest of the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 急遣元慶斷娑夷橋，其暮，吐蕃至，不克度。

translations.literal: He urgently sent Yuanqing to cut the Suoyi Bridge; that evening the Tibetans arrived and could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: He hurried Yuanqing to destroy the Suoyi Bridge. That evening the Tibetans arrived and could not cross.

sentences.zh: 橋長度一箭所及者，功一歲乃成。

translations.literal: The bridge was as long as an arrow's flight; it had taken a year to build.
translations.idiomatic: The bridge spanned a bowshot's length and had taken a year to construct.

sentences.zh: 八月，仙芝以小勃律王及妻自赤佛道還連雲堡，與令誠俱班師。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Xianzhi returned from the Chifo route to Lianyun Fort with the king of Lesser Bolü and his wife, and withdrew the army together with Lingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Xianzhi brought the king of Lesser Bolü and his wife back along the Chifo road to Lianyun Fort and withdrew with Lingcheng.

sentences.zh: 於是拂菻、大食諸胡七十二國皆震懾降附。

translations.literal: Thereupon seventy-two states of the Hu, including Byzantium and the Arabs, all trembled and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-two Hu states, from Byzantium to the Arabs, trembled and submitted.

sentences.zh: 仙芝遣判官王庭芬奏捷京師。

translations.literal: Xianzhi sent judge-advocate Wang Tingfen to report victory to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi sent his judge-advocate Wang Tingfen to announce victory in the capital.

sentences.zh: 軍至河西，靈察怒，不迎勞。

translations.literal: When the army reached Hexi, Lingcha was angry and did not come out to welcome or comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Hexi, Lingcha in anger refused to come out and welcome them.

sentences.zh: 既見，罵曰：「高麗奴，於闐使爾何從得之？

translations.literal: When they met, he cursed: "Koryo slave — by what means did the Khotan envoy obtain you?
translations.idiomatic: When they met he cursed him: "Koryo slave — how did a Khotan envoy come by the likes of you?

sentences.zh: 」仙芝懼，且謝曰：「中丞力也。

translations.literal: " Xianzhi was afraid and apologized: "It was the Vice Director's power.
translations.idiomatic: " Xianzhi was terrified and apologized, "It was all the Vice Director's doing.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「焉耆鎮守使、安西副都護、都知兵馬使，皆何從得之？

translations.literal: " He also said: "Garrison commander of Yanqi, deputy protector of Anxi, commandant of troops and horses — how were all these obtained?
translations.idiomatic: " Lingcha went on, "Commandant of Yanqi, deputy protector of Anxi, commander of troops and horses — how did you get all of those?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「亦中丞力也。

translations.literal: " He answered: "Also the Vice Director's power.
translations.idiomatic: " Xianzhi answered, "Those too were the Vice Director's doing.

sentences.zh: 」靈察曰：「審若此，捷書不待我而敢即奏，何邪？

translations.literal: " Lingcha said: "If that is truly so, why did you dare report victory without waiting for me?
translations.idiomatic: " Lingcha said, "If that is so, why did you dare send in the victory report before me?

sentences.zh: 奴當斬，顧新立功，故貸爾。

translations.literal: The slave ought to be beheaded; considering your fresh merit, I spare you.
translations.idiomatic: A slave like you deserves death, but for your fresh merit I let you off.

sentences.zh: 」仙芝不知所為。

translations.literal: " Xianzhi did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: " Xianzhi was at a loss.

sentences.zh: 令誠密言狀於朝，且曰：「仙芝立功而以憂死，後孰為朝廷用者？

translations.literal: Lingcheng secretly reported the situation to court and said: "Xianzhi achieved merit yet may die of worry — who afterward will serve the court?
translations.idiomatic: Lingcheng secretly reported the affair to court, adding, "Xianzhi wins battles yet may die of fear — who will serve the throne after this?

sentences.zh: 」帝乃擢仙芝鴻臚卿、假御史中丞，代靈察為四鎮節度使，而詔靈察還，靈察懼。

translations.literal: " The emperor then promoted Xianzhi to Minister of Ceremonial and acting Vice Censor-in-Chief, replacing Lingcha as military commissioner of the Four Garrisons, and ordered Lingcha to return; Lingcha was afraid.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then promoted Xianzhi to Minister of Ceremonial and acting Vice Censor-in-Chief, made him military commissioner of the Four Garrisons in Lingcha's place, and recalled Lingcha, who was terrified.

sentences.zh: 仙芝朝夕見，輒趨走，靈察益慚。

translations.literal: Whenever Xianzhi saw Lingcha morning or evening he would hurry and run; Lingcha grew all the more ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Xianzhi saw Lingcha he broke into a run; Lingcha grew only more humiliated.

sentences.zh: 副都護程千里、衙將畢思琛、行官王滔康懷順陳奉忠等皆嘗譖仙芝於靈察者。

translations.literal: Deputy Protector Cheng Qianli, yamen generals Bi Sichen, staff officer Wang Tao, Kang Huaishun, Chen Fengzhong, and others had all slandered Xianzhi to Lingcha.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Protector Cheng Qianli, yamen generals Bi Sichen, staff officer Wang Tao, Kang Huaishun, Chen Fengzhong, and others had all denounced Xianzhi to Lingcha.

sentences.zh: 既視事，呼千里嫚罵曰：「公面雖男兒，而心似婦女，何邪？

translations.literal: Once he took office he summoned Qianli and reviled him: "Your face is a man's, yet your heart is like a woman's — why?
translations.idiomatic: When he took office he called in Qianli and abused him: "You have a man's face and a woman's heart — what sort of thing is that?

sentences.zh: 」謂琛曰：「爾奪吾城東千石種田，憶之乎？

translations.literal: " He said to Sichen: "You seized my thousand-shi fields east of the city — do you remember?
translations.idiomatic: " To Sichen he said, "You took my thousand-shi fields east of the city — remember?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「公見賜者。

translations.literal: " He answered: "The Lord gave them to me.
translations.idiomatic: " Sichen replied, "Your Lordship gave them to me.

sentences.zh: 」仙芝曰：「爾時吾畏汝威，豈憐汝而賜邪？

translations.literal: " Xianzhi said: "At that time I feared your power — how would I have pitied you and given them?
translations.idiomatic: " Xianzhi said, "Then I feared you — I did not give them out of kindness.

sentences.zh: 」又召滔，欲捽辱。

translations.literal: " He also summoned Tao, intending to seize and humiliate him.
translations.idiomatic: " He also summoned Tao intending to humiliate him.

sentences.zh: 良久，皆釋，曰：「吾不恨矣。

translations.literal: After a long while he released them all and said: "I bear no grudge.
translations.idiomatic: After a long pause he released them all. "I bear no further grudge," he said.

sentences.zh: 」由是舉軍安之。

translations.literal: " From this the whole army was reassured.
translations.idiomatic: " From that day the whole army settled down.

sentences.zh: 俄加左金吾衛大將軍，與一子五品官。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was further made Grand General of the Left Golden Guard and one of his sons was given a fifth-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Grand General of the Left Golden Guard and one son received a fifth-rank post.

sentences.zh: 九載，討石國，其王車鼻施約降，仙芝為俘獻闕下，斬之，由是西域不服。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he campaigned against Shiguo; its king Chebish agreed to surrender, but Xianzhi took him captive and presented him at court, where he was beheaded; from this the Western Regions did not submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he attacked Shiguo. King Chebish offered surrender, but Xianzhi took him prisoner, sent him to court, and had him executed. The Western Regions never trusted him again.

sentences.zh: 其王子走大食，乞兵攻仙芝於怛邏斯城，以直其冤。

translations.literal: The prince fled to the Arabs and begged troops to attack Xianzhi at Talas city to avenge his wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The prince fled to the Arabs and begged an army to strike Xianzhi at Talas and avenge his father.

sentences.zh: 仙芝為人貪，破石，獲瑟瑟十餘斛、黃金五六橐駝、良馬寶玉甚眾，家貲累钜萬。

translations.literal: Xianzhi was greedy by nature; when he broke Shiguo he obtained more than ten hu of sese stones, five or six camel-loads of gold, and a great many fine horses and precious jades; his household wealth accumulated to vast sums.
