translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi was a greedy man. Sacking Shiguo he seized more than ten hu of sese gems, five or six camels' load of gold, and countless fine horses and jade. His household wealth swelled beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 然亦不甚愛惜，人有求輒與，不問幾何。

translations.literal: Yet he did not much cherish them; whenever anyone asked he gave, without asking how much.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he scarcely hoarded them — anyone who asked received a gift, with no count of the cost.

sentences.zh: 尋除武威太守，代安思順為河西節度使，群胡固留思順，更拜右羽林軍大將軍，封密雲郡公。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed prefect of Wuwei, replacing An Sishun as military commissioner of Hexi; the Hu masses firmly wished to keep Sishun; he was again made Grand General of the Right Feathered Forest Army and enfeoffed as Duke of Miyun Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made prefect of Wuwei and military commissioner of Hexi in An Sishun's place, but the Hu tribes wanted Sishun to stay. The court instead made Xianzhi Grand General of the Right Feathered Forest and Duke of Miyun Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祿山反，榮王為元帥，仙芝副之，領飛騎、彍騎及朔方等兵，出禁財募關輔士五萬，繼封常清東討。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, Prince Rong was made grand marshal and Xianzhi his deputy; he led Flying Cavalry, Expanded Cavalry, and Shuofang troops, spent imperial treasury funds to recruit fifty thousand Guanfu soldiers, and followed Feng Changqing east to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled, Prince Rong became grand marshal with Xianzhi as his deputy. Xianzhi led the Flying and Expanded Cavalry and Shuofang forces, spent palace funds to raise fifty thousand Guanfu troops, and marched east behind Feng Changqing.

sentences.zh: 帝禦勤政樓，引榮王受命，宴仙芝以下。

translations.literal: The emperor went to the Qinzheng Tower, invested Prince Rong, and feasted Xianzhi and those below.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to the Qinzheng Tower to invest Prince Rong and feast Xianzhi and his officers.

sentences.zh: 帝又幸望春亭勞遣，詔監門將軍邊令誠監軍。

translations.literal: The emperor again visited Wangchun Pavilion to see them off with comfort, and ordered Gate Guard General Bian Lingcheng to oversee the army.
translations.idiomatic: He again saw them off from Wangchun Pavilion and appointed Gate Guard General Bian Lingcheng army overseer.

sentences.zh: 次陝郡，而常清敗還。

translations.literal: They halted at Shaan Commandery while Changqing returned defeated.
translations.idiomatic: They halted at Shaan Commandery as Changqing came back in defeat.

sentences.zh: 仙芝急，乃開太原倉，悉以所有賜士卒，焚其餘，引兵趨潼關。

translations.literal: Xianzhi in haste opened the Taiyuan granary, gave all its contents to the soldiers, burned the remainder, and led troops toward Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi in panic opened the Taiyuan granary, gave everything to the troops, burned what remained, and raced for Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 會賊至，甲仗資糧委於道，彌數百里。

translations.literal: When the rebels arrived, armor, weapons, and provisions were abandoned along the road for several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels closed in, arms and provisions littered the road for hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 既至關，勒兵繕守具，士氣稍稍復振。

translations.literal: Once they reached the pass they drilled the troops and repaired defenses; morale gradually revived.
translations.idiomatic: At the pass they re-formed the ranks and repaired the defenses, and spirit slowly returned.

sentences.zh: 賊攻關不得入，乃引還。

translations.literal: The rebels attacked the pass but could not enter and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels assaulted the pass, failed to break in, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 初，令誠數私於仙芝，仙芝不應，因言其逗撓狀以激帝，且云：「常清以賊搖眾，而仙芝棄陝地數百里，朘盜稟賜。

translations.literal: At first Lingcheng had repeatedly spoken privately to Xianzhi; Xianzhi did not respond; he therefore reported his delay and shirking to provoke the emperor, and also said: "Changqing was shaken by the rebels' numbers, while Xianzhi abandoned several hundred li of Shaan territory and embezzled the grain gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Lingcheng had repeatedly tried to win Xianzhi over in private; Xianzhi ignored him. Lingcheng then reported delay and cowardice to enrage the emperor, adding, "Changqing lost heart before the rebels, while Xianzhi abandoned hundreds of li in Shaan and stole the grain meant for the troops.

sentences.zh: 」帝大怒，使令誠即軍中斬之。

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly angered and ordered Lingcheng to behead him in the army at once.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor flew into a rage and ordered Lingcheng to execute him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 令誠已斬常清，陳屍於蘧祼。

translations.literal: Lingcheng had already beheaded Changqing and displayed the corpse at Quanluo.
translations.idiomatic: Lingcheng had already killed Changqing and displayed his body at Quanluo.

sentences.zh: 仙芝自外至，令誠以陌刀百人自從，曰：'大夫亦有命。

translations.literal: Xianzhi came in from outside; Lingcheng followed with a hundred men bearing mo dao and said: 'The Grand Marshal also has orders.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi arrived from outside. Lingcheng came with a hundred men carrying mo dao blades and said, "The Grand Marshal has orders too.

sentences.zh: 」仙芝遽下，曰：「我退，罪也，死不敢辭。

translations.literal: " Xianzhi hurriedly dismounted and said: "My retreat is a crime; death I dare not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: " Xianzhi dismounted at once. "Retreat was my crime," he said. "I do not refuse death.

sentences.zh: 然以我為盜頡資糧，誣也。

translations.literal: Yet to call me a thief who stole provisions is slander.
translations.idiomatic: But to call me a thief who stole rations is a lie.

sentences.zh: 」謂令誠曰：「上天下地，三軍皆在，君豈不知？

translations.literal: " He said to Lingcheng: "Heaven and earth, the whole army is here — do you not know?
translations.idiomatic: " He turned to Lingcheng. "Heaven and earth bear witness — the whole army is here. Do you not know?

sentences.zh: 」又顧麾下曰：「我募若輩，本欲破賊取重賞，而賊勢方銳，故遷延至此，亦以固關也。

translations.literal: " He also looked at his followers and said: "I recruited you originally to break the rebels and win great rewards; the rebels' momentum was just sharp, so I delayed until now — also to hold the pass firm.
translations.idiomatic: " He addressed his men: "I raised you to crush the rebels and win rich rewards. Their momentum was fierce, so I held back — also to keep the pass secure.

sentences.zh: 我有罪，若輩可言；

translations.literal: If I am guilty, you may speak;
translations.idiomatic: If I am guilty, speak up;

sentences.zh: 不爾，當呼枉。

translations.literal: if not, you should cry injustice.
translations.idiomatic: if not, cry out that I am wronged.

sentences.zh: 」軍中咸呼曰：「枉！

translations.literal: " The whole army cried: "Wronged!
translations.idiomatic: " The whole army roared, "Wronged!

sentences.zh: 」其聲殷地。

translations.literal: " The sound shook the earth.
translations.idiomatic: " The shout shook the ground.

sentences.zh: 仙芝視常清屍曰：「公，我所引拔，又代吾為節度，今與公同死，豈命歟！

translations.literal: Xianzhi looked at Changqing's corpse and said: "Sir, you were my protégé and later replaced me as commissioner — now to die with you, is it fate!
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi looked at Changqing's body and said, "You were the man I raised up and who succeeded me as commissioner — to die with you now, is this fate?

sentences.zh: 」遂就死。

translations.literal: " He then submitted to death.
translations.idiomatic: " He then went to his death.

sentences.zh: 封常清

translations.literal: Feng Changqing
translations.idiomatic: Feng Changqing

sentences.zh: 封常清，蒲州猗氏人。

translations.literal: Feng Changqing, a man of Yishi in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Changqing was a native of Yishi in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 外祖教之讀書，多所該究。

translations.literal: His maternal grandfather taught him to read; he mastered many subjects.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal grandfather taught him letters, and he gained wide learning.

sentences.zh: 然孤貧，年過三十，未有名。

translations.literal: Yet he was orphaned and poor; past thirty he had no reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor, he passed thirty without a name.

sentences.zh: 夫蒙靈察為四鎮節度使，以高仙芝為都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: Fumeng Lingcha was military commissioner of the Four Garrisons and made Gao Xianzhi commandant of troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Fumeng Lingcha commanded the Four Garrisons and appointed Gao Xianzhi commander of troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 嘗出軍，奏傔從三十餘人，衣褷鮮明，常清慨然投牒請豫。

translations.literal: Once when going out on campaign he memorialized more than thirty attendants in bright dress; Changqing in indignation submitted a petition asking to join.
translations.idiomatic: Once, setting out on campaign, Xianzhi listed more than thirty brightly dressed attendants. Changqing in frustration submitted a petition to join them.

sentences.zh: 常清素瘠，又腳跛，仙芝陋其貌，不納。

translations.literal: Changqing had always been thin and also lame; Xianzhi despised his appearance and did not accept him.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing was gaunt and lame. Xianzhi disliked his looks and turned him away.

sentences.zh: 明日復至，仙芝謝曰：「傔已足，何庸復來？

translations.literal: The next day he came again; Xianzhi apologized: "Attendants are already sufficient — why come again?
translations.idiomatic: He came again the next day. Xianzhi apologized, "I have enough attendants — why come again?

sentences.zh: 」常清怒曰：「我慕公義，願事鞭靮，故無媒自前，公何見拒深乎？

translations.literal: " Changqing angrily said: "I admire your righteousness and wish to serve at your bridle — therefore I came without a go-between; why do you reject me so deeply?
translations.idiomatic: " Changqing flared up. "I admire your honor and came unbidden to serve at your bridle. Why reject me so harshly?

sentences.zh: 以貌取士，恐失之子羽。

translations.literal: To choose men by appearance — I fear you will lose a Ziyu.
translations.idiomatic: Choose men by looks and you may miss another Ziyu.

sentences.zh: 公其念之。

translations.literal: My lord, consider this.
translations.idiomatic: Think on that, my lord.

sentences.zh: 」仙芝猶未納，乃日候門下，仙芝不得已，竄名傔中。

translations.literal: " Xianzhi still did not accept; he then waited daily at the gate; Xianzhi had no choice and slipped his name among the attendants.
translations.idiomatic: " Xianzhi still refused, so Changqing waited at his gate every day until Xianzhi, unable to refuse further, slipped his name onto the attendant roll.

sentences.zh: 會達奚諸部叛，自黑山西趣碎葉，有詔邀擊。

translations.literal: When the Daxi tribes rebelled and moved from Black Mountain toward Suyab, an edict ordered interception.
translations.idiomatic: When the Daxi tribes rebelled and marched from Black Mountain toward Suyab, the court ordered them intercepted.

sentences.zh: 靈察使仙芝以二千騎追躡。

translations.literal: Lingcha had Xianzhi pursue with two thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Lingcha sent Xianzhi after them with two thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 達奚行遠，人馬疲，禽馘略盡。

translations.literal: The Daxi had marched far; men and horses were weary; captives and heads were nearly all taken.
translations.idiomatic: The Daxi had marched far and were exhausted; Xianzhi took prisoners and heads until almost none remained.

sentences.zh: 常清於幕下潛作捷布，具記井泉次舍、克賊形勢謀略，條最明審。

translations.literal: Changqing secretly drafted a victory dispatch in the tent, fully recording wells and springs, halting places, the enemy's disposition, and stratagems, all itemized with clarity.
translations.idiomatic: In camp Changqing secretly drafted a victory report listing every well, halt, enemy movement, and stratagem in meticulous detail.

sentences.zh: 仙芝取讀之，皆意所欲出，乃大駭，即用之。

translations.literal: Xianzhi took and read it; all were exactly what he had wished to say; he was greatly startled and immediately used it.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi read it and found every line matched what he himself would have written. Astonished, he sent it at once.

sentences.zh: 軍還，靈察迎勞，仙芝已去奴襪帶刀，而判官劉眺、獨孤峻爭問：「向捷布誰作者？

translations.literal: When the army returned Lingcha came to welcome them; Xianzhi had already removed his servant's socks and belted on a sword; judge-advocates Liu Tiao and Dugu Jun eagerly asked: "Who wrote that victory dispatch?
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, Lingcha came to welcome them. Xianzhi had already cast off his servant's dress and wore a sword. Judge-advocates Liu Tiao and Dugu Jun asked at once, "Who wrote that victory report?

sentences.zh: 公幕下安得此人？

translations.literal: How does your staff hold such a man?
translations.idiomatic: Where did you find such a man on your staff?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「吾傔封常清也。

translations.literal: " He answered: "My attendant Feng Changqing.
translations.idiomatic: " Xianzhi answered, "My attendant Feng Changqing.

sentences.zh: 」眺等驚，進揖常清坐，與語，異之，遂知名。

translations.literal: " Tiao and the others were startled; they advanced, bowed, and seated Changqing, spoke with him, and were impressed; he thereby became known.
translations.idiomatic: " Tiao and the others were stunned. They bowed Changqing to a seat, talked with him, and were deeply impressed. His name spread from that day.

sentences.zh: 以功授疊州戍主，仍為判官。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed garrison commander of Diezhou and remained judge-advocate.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made garrison commander of Diezhou and kept as judge-advocate.

sentences.zh: 仙芝破小勃律，代靈察為安西節度使，常清以從戰有勞，擢慶王府錄事參軍事，為節度判官。

translations.literal: When Xianzhi broke Lesser Bolü and replaced Lingcha as Anxi military commissioner, Changqing for following in battle with merit was promoted to recorder of the Prince of Qing's mansion and made commissioner judge-advocate.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzhi conquered Lesser Bolü and replaced Lingcha as Anxi commissioner, Changqing was promoted to recorder in the Prince of Qing's household and made the commissioner's judge-advocate for his campaign service.

sentences.zh: 仙芝征討，常知後務。

translations.literal: Whenever Xianzhi campaigned, Changqing regularly managed rear affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On every campaign Xianzhi left the rear to Changqing.

sentences.zh: 常清才而果，胸無疑事。

translations.literal: Changqing was talented and resolute; no doubt lingered in his breast.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing was able and decisive, with never a doubt in his mind.

sentences.zh: 仙芝委家事于郎將鄭德詮，其乳母子也，威動軍中。

translations.literal: Xianzhi entrusted household affairs to Colonel Zheng Dequan, son of his wet nurse, whose authority shook the army.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi left household affairs to Colonel Zheng Dequan, his wet nurse's son, whose power intimidated the whole army.

sentences.zh: 常清嘗自外還，諸將前謁。

translations.literal: Changqing once returned from outside and the generals came forward to pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Changqing returned from an errand, the generals came out to greet him.

sentences.zh: 德詮見常清始貴，易之，走馬突常清騶士去。

translations.literal: Dequan, seeing Changqing newly honored, treated him lightly, galloped his horse and charged through Changqing's outriders.
translations.idiomatic: Dequan, seeing Changqing's new rank, showed disrespect, spurring his horse through Changqing's escort.

sentences.zh: 常清命左右引德詮至廷中，門輒閉，因離席曰：「吾起細微，中丞公過聽，以主留事，郎將安得無禮？

translations.literal: Changqing ordered his attendants to bring Dequan into the courtyard; the gate was closed; he rose from his seat and said: "I rose from humble origins; the Vice Director overestimated me and put me in charge of affairs — how dare a colonel be rude?
translations.idiomatic: Changqing had his men bring Dequan into the court and shut the gate. Rising from his seat he said, "I came from nothing; the Vice Director trusted me with command — how dare a colonel show such insolence?

sentences.zh: 」因叱曰：「須暫假郎將死，以肅吾軍。

translations.literal: " He then shouted: "I must borrow the colonel's death for a time to discipline my army.
translations.idiomatic: " He cried, "I must take the colonel's life for a moment to restore order in this army.

sentences.zh: 」因杖死，以面僕地曳出之。

translations.literal: " He then beat him to death and dragged him out face down along the ground.
translations.idiomatic: " He had him beaten to death and dragged out facedown.

sentences.zh: 仙芝妻及乳母哭門外救請，不能得，遽以狀白仙芝，仙芝驚，及見常清，憚其公，不敢讓。

translations.literal: Xianzhi's wife and wet nurse wept outside the gate begging for his life but could not save him; they hurriedly reported to Xianzhi; Xianzhi was startled; when he saw Changqing he feared his public rectitude and did not reproach him.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi's wife and wet nurse wailed at the gate in vain. They rushed word to Xianzhi, who was shocked; when he faced Changqing he dared not rebuke him for his stern justice.

sentences.zh: 常清亦不謝。

translations.literal: Changqing also did not apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing offered no apology.

sentences.zh: 會大將有罪，又殺二人，軍中莫不股栗。

translations.literal: When a great general was guilty he killed two more men; throughout the army none did not tremble in the thighs.
translations.idiomatic: When a senior officer offended him he killed two more men, and the whole army shook with fear.

sentences.zh: 仙芝節度河西，復請為判官。

translations.literal: When Xianzhi was commissioner of Hexi he again asked that Changqing serve as judge-advocate.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzhi took command of Hexi he again asked Changqing to serve as his judge-advocate.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢安西副大都護、安西四鎮節度副大使，知節度事。

translations.literal: After some time he was promoted to deputy grand protector of Anxi and deputy grand commissioner of the Anxi Four Garrisons, managing commissioner affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was made deputy grand protector of Anxi and deputy grand commissioner of the Four Garrisons, acting commissioner in all but name.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改北庭都護，持節伊西節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to protector of Beiting and made military commissioner of Yi and Xi with the staff of authority.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to protector of Beiting and military commissioner of Yi and Xi with full insignia of command.

sentences.zh: 常清性勤儉，耐勞苦，出軍乘騾，私廄裁二馬，賞罰分明。

translations.literal: Changqing was by nature diligent and frugal, enduring hardship; on campaign he rode a mule; his private stable held only two horses; rewards and punishments were clear.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal and tireless by nature, he rode a mule on campaign and kept only two horses in his private stable. Rewards and punishments were exact.

sentences.zh: 天寶末入朝，而安祿山反，帝引見，問何策以討賊。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao he entered court; An Lushan rebelled; the emperor received him and asked what plan could suppress the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao era he came to court just as An Lushan rebelled. The emperor summoned him and asked how to defeat the rebels.

sentences.zh: 常清見帝憂，因大言曰：「天下太平久，人不知戰。

translations.literal: Changqing, seeing the emperor's worry, therefore spoke boldly: "The realm has been at peace long; men do not know war.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the emperor's distress, Changqing spoke boldly: "The empire has known peace so long that men have forgotten war.

sentences.zh: 然事有逆順，勢有奇變，臣請馳至東京，悉府庫募驍勇，挑馬箠度河，計日取逆胡首以獻闕下。

translations.literal: Yet affairs have opposition and accord, and situations have strange turns; I ask to gallop to the Eastern Capital, exhaust the treasuries to recruit the brave, whip our horses across the river, and within counted days bring the rebel Hu's head to present below the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yet fortune turns, and stratagems still avail. Let me ride to the Eastern Capital, empty the treasuries to raise brave men, lash our horses across the river, and within days bring the rebel's head to the palace.

sentences.zh: 」天子壯之。

translations.literal: " The Son of Heaven was heartened.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor took heart.

sentences.zh: 明日，以常清為范陽節度副大使，乘驛赴東京。

translations.literal: The next day Changqing was made deputy military commissioner of Fanyang and rode post-horses to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was made deputy military commissioner of Fanyang and galloped by post relay to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 常清募兵得六萬人，然皆市井庸保，乃部分旗幟，斷河陽橋以守。

translations.literal: Changqing recruited sixty thousand men, but all were market loafers and hired guards; he therefore arranged banners and flags and broke the Heyang Bridge to hold.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing raised sixty thousand men, but they were shopkeepers and day laborers. He arrayed banners and destroyed the Heyang Bridge to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 賊移書平原，令太守顏真卿以兵七千防河。

translations.literal: The rebels sent a letter to Pingyuan ordering Prefect Yan Zhenqing to defend the river with seven thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels wrote to Pingyuan ordering Prefect Yan Zhenqing to hold the river with seven thousand men.

sentences.zh: 真卿馳使司兵參軍事李平入奏。

translations.literal: Zhenqing sent his army registrar Li Ping in haste to report to court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing dispatched his army registrar Li Ping to report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 常清取平表發視，即倚帳作書遺真卿，勸堅守，且傳購祿山檄數十函與之，真卿得，以分曉諸郡。

translations.literal: Changqing took Ping's memorial, opened and read it, then leaning on his tent wrote a letter to Zhenqing urging steadfast defense, and also transmitted several dozen copies of Lushan's proclamations with rewards for capture; Zhenqing received them and distributed them to enlighten the commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing read Li Ping's dispatch, then from his tent wrote Zhenqing urging him to stand firm and sent dozens of copies of Lushan's bounty proclamations. Zhenqing circulated them through the provinces.

sentences.zh: 祿山度河，陷滎陽，入罌子谷，先驅至葵園。

translations.literal: Lushan crossed the river, took Xingyang, entered Yingzi Valley; the vanguard reached Sunflower Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan crossed the river, captured Xingyang, entered Yingzi Valley, and his vanguard reached Sunflower Garden.

sentences.zh: 常清使驍騎拒之，殺拓羯數十百人。

translations.literal: Changqing sent fierce cavalry to resist them and killed several tens or hundreds of Tujue.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing sent his best cavalry to meet them and killed scores of Tujue warriors.

sentences.zh: 賊大軍至，常清不能禦，退入上東門，戰不利。

translations.literal: The rebel main army arrived; Changqing could not hold them off, withdrew into the Upper East Gate, and the battle went badly.
translations.idiomatic: When the main rebel force arrived Changqing could not hold. He fell back to the Upper East Gate and lost the fight.

sentences.zh: 賊鼓而進，劫官吏。

translations.literal: The rebels beat drums and advanced, seizing officials.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels advanced to the drum and seized the officials.

sentences.zh: 再戰於都亭驛，又不勝，引兵守宣仁門，復敗。

translations.literal: They fought again at Duting Post Station and again did not win; he led troops to hold Xuanren Gate and was defeated again.
translations.idiomatic: They fought again at Duting Station and lost again, then tried to hold Xuanren Gate and were beaten once more.

sentences.zh: 乃自提象門出，伐大木塞道以殿，至谷水，西奔陝。

translations.literal: He then went out through Elephant Gate himself, felled great trees to block the road as rear guard, reached Gu River, and fled west to Shaan.
translations.idiomatic: He slipped out through Elephant Gate, felled trees to block pursuit, reached Gu River, and fled west to Shaan.

sentences.zh: 語高仙芝曰：「賊銳甚，難與爭鋒。

translations.literal: He told Gao Xianzhi: "The rebels are very sharp; it is hard to contend with their edge.
translations.idiomatic: He told Gao Xianzhi, "The rebels are at their peak — we cannot meet them head on.

sentences.zh: 潼關無兵，一夫奔突則京師危，不如急守潼關。

translations.literal: Tong Pass has no troops; if one man breaks through in a rush the capital will be in peril — better to hurry and hold Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Pass is barely manned. One breakthrough and the capital falls. We must hold the pass at once.

sentences.zh: 」仙芝從之。

translations.literal: " Xianzhi followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " Xianzhi agreed.

sentences.zh: 敗書聞，帝削常清官，使白衣隸仙芝軍效力。

translations.literal: When news of defeat arrived, the emperor stripped Changqing of rank and had him serve in plain clothes under Xianzhi's army.
translations.idiomatic: When word of defeat reached the court, the emperor stripped Changqing of rank and made him serve in common dress under Xianzhi.

sentences.zh: 仙芝使衣黑衣監左右部軍。

translations.literal: Xianzhi had him wear black clothes to oversee the left and right divisions of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi put him in black to supervise the left and right wings of the army.

sentences.zh: 及邊令誠以詔書至，示之，常清曰：「吾所以不死者，恐汙國家節，受戮賊手。

translations.literal: When Bian Lingcheng arrived with the imperial edict and showed it, Changqing said: "The reason I did not die was fear of staining the state's honor by dying at rebel hands.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian Lingcheng arrived with the edict, Changqing said, "I stayed alive only so I would not die a traitor's death and stain the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 今死乃甘心。」

translations.literal: Now to die is my heart's content."
translations.idiomatic: Now I can die content."

sentences.zh: 始，常清敗，徑入關，欲見上陳討賊事。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Changqing was defeated he went straight into the pass wishing to see the emperor and set forth plans against the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after his defeat, Changqing had entered the pass intending to see the emperor and explain the campaign.

sentences.zh: 至渭南，有詔赴潼關。

translations.literal: Reaching Weinan, there was an edict ordering him to Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: At Weinan an edict ordered him to Tong Pass instead.

sentences.zh: 常清憂懼，為表以謝，且言：「自東京陷，三遣使表論成敗，不得對。

translations.literal: Changqing was anxious and afraid; he wrote a memorial to apologize and also said: "Since the Eastern Capital fell I have three times sent envoys with memorials on success and failure but received no audience.
translations.idiomatic: Anxious and afraid, he submitted a memorial of apology, adding, "Since the Eastern Capital fell I have sent three memorials on the course of the war and received no answer.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「臣死後，望陛下無輕此賊，則社稷安。

translations.literal: " He also said: "After my death I hope Your Majesty will not underestimate this rebel — then the altars of state will be secure.
translations.idiomatic: " He also wrote, "After I die, do not underestimate this rebel, and the realm will endure.

sentences.zh: 」至是臨刑，以表授令誠而死。

translations.literal: " At the moment of execution he handed the memorial to Lingcheng and died.
translations.idiomatic: " At the block he gave the memorial to Lingcheng and went to his death.

sentences.zh: 人多哀之。

translations.literal: Many mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Many grieved for him.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：祿山裒百鬥驍虜，乘天下忘戰，主德耄勤，故提戈內噪，人情崩潰。

translations.literal: The comment says: Lushan gathered a hundred battles' worth of fierce barbarians, seized upon the realm's forgetfulness of war and the ruler's aged diligence, therefore raised weapons and clamored within, and human hearts collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: Lushan mustered fierce warriors hardened in a hundred fights, exploited a realm that had forgotten war and a ruler grown old in pleasure, raised arms within the empire, and men's hearts gave way.

sentences.zh: 常清乃驅市人數萬以嬰賊鋒，一戰不勝，即奪爵土。

translations.literal: Changqing then drove tens of thousands of market men to meet the rebels' edge; after one battle lost he was stripped of rank and fief.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing drove tens of thousands of townsfolk against the rebel spears; one defeat cost him rank and lands.

sentences.zh: 欲入關見天子論成敗事，使者三輩上書，皆不報，回斬於軍。

translations.literal: Wishing to enter the pass and see the Son of Heaven to discuss success and failure, three envoys submitted memorials — none were answered — and he was beheaded on return in the army.
translations.idiomatic: He tried to reach the emperor to report the truth; three messengers carried memorials and none was answered. He was executed on his return to camp.

sentences.zh: 仙芝棄陝守關，遏賊西勢，以喪地被誅。

translations.literal: Xianzhi abandoned Shaan to hold the pass, checked the rebels' westward momentum, yet was executed for lost territory.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi gave up Shaan to hold the pass and checked the rebel advance west, yet was killed for yielding ground.

sentences.zh: 玄宗雖為左右蒙瞽，然荒奪其明亦甚矣。

translations.literal: Although Emperor Xuanzong was blinded by those around him, he had also abandoned his clarity to a very great degree.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong was deceived by his courtiers, but he had also surrendered his judgment almost completely.

sentences.zh: 卒使叛將得藉口，執翰以降賊。

translations.literal: In the end rebel generals gained their pretext and seized Han to surrender to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the rebel generals found their excuse, seized Ge Shu Han, and delivered him to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，非天熟其惡，使亂四海，舉黔首而殘之邪！

translations.literal: Alas — was it not Heaven ripening their evil, making them disorder the four seas and slaughter the black-haired people!
translations.idiomatic: Alas — had Heaven not ripened their wickedness, driving them to ravage the empire and butcher the people!

sentences.zh: 彼二將奚誅焉？

translations.literal: Why were those two generals put to death?
translations.idiomatic: What crime deserved death for those two generals?
